heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What determines the physical state of a homogeneous solution such as an alloy or an aqueous salt solution?
options: The physical state of the solute
The physical state of the solvent
The molar mass of the solute
The chemical formula of the solute
solution: B - The physical state of the solvent The solvent is the component that determines the phase. Water gives an aqueous liquid solution, while the solid metallic solvent in brass gives a solid solution.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Brass containing 70% Cu and 30% Zn by mass is classified as which type of solution?
solution: D - Solid in solid Zinc and copper are both solids under ordinary conditions. Zinc is the solute and copper is the solvent, so brass is a solid-in-solid solution.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A solution contains 24 g of a 60 g mol<sup>-1</sup> solute and 108 g of water. With M(H<sub>2</sub>O) = 18 g mol<sup>-1</sup>, what is the mole fraction of water?
solution: C - 15/16 Solute = 24/60 = 0.40 mol and water = 108/18 = 6.00 mol. The mole fraction of water is 6.00/(6.00 + 0.40) = 15/16.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Of 100 g of a 12% (w/w) KCl solution, 25 g of water evaporates. No KCl is lost or precipitated. What is the new mass percentage of KCl?
solution: A - 16% The original sample contains 12 g of KCl. After evaporation the solution weighs 75 g, so 100 × 12/75 = 16%.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A 300 mL sample of 0.20 M NaCl is mixed with 200 mL of 0.50 M NaCl. If volumes are additive, what is the molarity of the mixture?
solution: D - 0.32 M The two samples supply 0.300 × 0.20 + 0.200 × 0.50 = 0.160 mol. Divide by 0.500 L to get 0.32 M.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A 1.00 mol kg<sup>-1</sup> aqueous glucose solution contains 1.00 kg of water. Its density is 1.18 g mL<sup>-1</sup> and M(glucose) = 180 g mol<sup>-1</sup>. What is its molarity?
solution: B - 1.00 M One mole of glucose adds 180 g to 1000 g of water. At 1.18 g mL<sup>-1</sup> the 1180 g solution occupies 1.00 L, so its molarity is 1.00 M.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A sample has a solute mass fraction of 3.0 × 10<sup>-7</sup>. How many micrograms of solute are present in 1.00 kg of sample?
solution: D - 300 μg Multiply 1.00 kg by 3.0 × 10<sup>-7</sup>. Since 1 kg = 10<sup>9</sup> μg, the solute mass is 300 μg.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Equal volumes of ethanol and water are mixed and the final volume is smaller than the sum of the initial volumes. Which pair can be calculated from the component masses and their molar masses without using the final volume?
solution: B - Mole fraction and mass percentage Mass percentage uses solute mass divided by total mass. Mole fraction uses component moles divided by total moles. Both can be found without the final volume.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A solution cooled below its saturation temperature retains more dissolved solute than its equilibrium solubility. What often happens on adding a small crystal of the solute?
options: The solvent crystallises while all solute remains dissolved.
Excess solute crystallises until the solution is saturated.
The equilibrium solubility increases at the same temperature.
solution: C - Excess solute crystallises until the solution is saturated. The seed crystal provides a surface for solute crystallisation. Excess solute separates until the dissolved concentration falls to the equilibrium saturation value.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A plot of gas partial pressure (vertical axis) against its mole fraction in water (horizontal axis) is linear at fixed temperature. What does a steeper slope imply?
options: A higher Henry constant and a larger mole fraction at the same pressure
A lower Henry constant and a smaller mole fraction at the same pressure
A lower Henry constant and a larger mole fraction at the same pressure
A higher Henry constant and a smaller mole fraction at the same pressure
solution: D - A higher Henry constant and a smaller mole fraction at the same pressure Henry’s law gives p = KHx, so the slope is KH. At fixed p, a greater KH gives a smaller x = p/KH.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why is a helium-containing breathing mixture preferred over ordinary compressed air for deep-sea diving in the NCERT example?
options: Helium raises the partial pressure of nitrogen at the same total pressure.
Helium helps reduce the quantity of nitrogen that can dissolve in blood under pressure.
Helium makes nitrogen more soluble in blood.
Helium keeps total gas pressure equal to surface pressure at all depths.
solution: B - Helium helps reduce the quantity of nitrogen that can dissolve in blood under pressure. Replacing part of the nitrogen with helium reduces the nitrogen partial pressure and hence the amount of nitrogen dissolved in the blood under pressure.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: At fixed temperature an ideal binary liquid contains xA = 0.30. The pure vapour pressures of A and B are 90 and 30 kPa. What is the partial pressure of B above the solution?
solution: C - 21 kPa The liquid mole fraction of B is 1 − 0.30 = 0.70. Raoult’s law gives p(B) = 0.70 × 30 = 21 kPa.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: At a fixed temperature, pure A has a vapour pressure of 40 kPa and pure B 60 kPa. An ideal solution of these liquids has a total vapour pressure of 56 kPa. What is xB?

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A non-volatile solute lowers the vapour pressure of a solvent from 50.0 to 48.5 kPa. What is the solvent mole fraction if Raoult’s law holds?
solution: A - 0.970 The solute contributes no vapour pressure. From p = xp°, the solvent mole fraction is 48.5/50.0 = 0.970.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In an ideal solution a non-volatile solute has mole fraction 0.040. If the pure solvent vapour pressure is 75 kPa, what is the absolute lowering in vapour pressure?
solution: B - 3.0 kPa The absolute decrease is x(solute)p° = 0.040 × 75 = 3.0 kPa.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A sample is prepared by mixing two liquids whose unlike attractions are similar to their respective like attractions. Which observation supports ideal behaviour?
options: A sharp maximum in boiling temperature appears at an intermediate composition.
Vapour pressure consistently lies below the Raoult-law prediction.
Total vapour pressure follows the mole-fraction-weighted pure pressures throughout the composition range.
The liquids evolve substantial heat on mixing.
solution: C - Total vapour pressure follows the mole-fraction-weighted pure pressures throughout the composition range. For an ideal binary solution p(total) = x(A)p°(A) + x(B)p°(B) across the composition range. Comparable unlike and like attractions support this behaviour.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: At the same temperature, the measured total vapour pressure of a mixture is 86 kPa. The Raoult-law prediction is 73 kPa. Which inference is most consistent with the data?
options: The mixture shows negative deviation and the molecules escape less readily than from an ideal mixture.
The mixture is ideal because both components are volatile.
The mixture shows negative deviation and its molecules escape more readily than from an ideal mixture.
The mixture shows positive deviation and the molecules escape more readily than from an ideal mixture.
solution: D - The mixture shows positive deviation and the molecules escape more readily than from an ideal mixture. The measured pressure exceeds the ideal value by 13 kPa. More molecules escape to the vapour, so the deviation is positive.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Ethanol and acetone show positive deviation from Raoult’s law. Which molecular change accounts for this in the textbook model?
options: Acetone disrupts some of the hydrogen bonding between ethanol molecules.
Acetone produces ions that bind ethanol strongly.
Ethanol and acetone react to make a less volatile compound.
Acetone greatly strengthens the hydrogen bonding between ethanol molecules.
solution: A - Acetone disrupts some of the hydrogen bonding between ethanol molecules. Acetone disrupts some ethanol–ethanol hydrogen bonds. In the textbook example the resulting weaker average attractions favour escape into the vapour.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A dilute solution of 0.20 mol of a non-electrolyte contains 0.50 kg of solvent with a normal boiling point of 80.0°C and Kb = 2.50 K kg mol<sup>-1</sup>. What is the boiling point at 1 atm?
solution: B - 81.0°C Molality = 0.20/0.50 = 0.40 mol kg<sup>-1</sup>. The elevation is 2.50 × 0.40 = 1.0 K, giving 81.0°C.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why does a solution of a non-volatile solute in water need a higher temperature to boil at 1 atm than pure water?
options: At the pure water boiling temperature, the solution’s vapour pressure is below 1 atm.
At the pure water boiling temperature, the solution’s vapour pressure is above 1 atm.
The non-volatile solute contributes enough vapour pressure to reach 1 atm sooner.
The solution boils when its vapour pressure first becomes zero.
solution: A - At the pure water boiling temperature, the solution’s vapour pressure is below 1 atm. At pure water’s boiling point, the dissolved non-volatile solute lowers the vapour pressure below 1 atm. Heating further brings it up to 1 atm.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which sample has the greatest boiling-point elevation? Assume ideal behaviour, the same solvent, and complete dissociation of the salts.
solution: C - 0.15 mol kg<sup>-1</sup> Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> Compare im for KCl, CaCl<sub>2</sub>, Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> and glucose: 0.40, 0.36, 0.45 and 0.40 mol kg<sup>-1</sup> respectively. Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> gives the largest elevation.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: An aqueous solution of 0.050 mol kg<sup>-1</sup> K<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> has a freezing-point depression of 0.2511 K. Given Kf = 1.86 K kg mol<sup>-1</sup>, what is its observed van’t Hoff factor?

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A 0.25 mol kg<sup>-1</sup> aqueous solution of a non-electrolyte has Kf = 1.86 and Kb = 0.52 K kg mol<sup>-1</sup>. By how much does the interval between its boiling and freezing points increase compared with pure water at the same pressure?
solution: D - 0.595 K The boiling point rises by 0.52 × 0.25 = 0.130 K and the freezing point falls by 1.86 × 0.25 = 0.465 K. The interval increases by 0.595 K.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Two ideal dilute solutions of the same non-electrolyte at the same temperature exert equal osmotic pressures. One has half the volume of the other. What follows?
options: Their molarities are equal, and both contain the same number of moles.
Their molarities are equal, and the smaller solution contains half as many moles.
The smaller solution has twice the molarity and the same number of moles.
The smaller solution has half the molarity and half the number of moles.
solution: B - Their molarities are equal, and the smaller solution contains half as many moles. Equal Π at the same T gives equal C from Π = CRT. Since n = CV, half the volume contains half as many moles.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A red blood cell is placed in a solution hypotonic to its fluid. What is the initial net movement of water?
options: Water is converted into a dissolved solute.
solution: C - Into the cell The surrounding solution is hypotonic, so its solute-particle concentration is lower than the cell’s. The initial net flow of water is into the cell.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A 4.00 g sample of a non-electrolyte polymer is dissolved to make 0.500 L of solution. It exerts Π = 0.0246 atm at 300 K. With R = 0.082 L atm mol<sup>-1</sup> K<sup>-1</sup>, what is its molar mass?

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: When a salt solution exerts an osmotic pressure of 5.0 atm against pure water, what happens if a pressure difference of exactly 5.0 atm is applied to the salt-solution side at the same temperature?
options: There is no net flow of solvent through an ideal semipermeable membrane.
Water moves from the solution into pure water by reverse osmosis.
Water crosses from the pure side as rapidly as before applying pressure.
Salt ions move through the membrane until both sides have equal salinity.
solution: A - There is no net flow of solvent through an ideal semipermeable membrane. Osmotic pressure is the pressure difference needed to stop the net flow of solvent. Reverse osmosis would require a pressure difference above 5.0 atm.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A solute of known normal molar mass trimerises partially. The observed van’t Hoff factor is 0.80. What fraction of the original solute molecules has participated in trimer formation?
solution: C - 0.30 If fraction α trimerises, the particle ratio is (1 − α) + α/3 = 1 − 2α/3. Setting it equal to 0.80 gives α = 0.30.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A weak monoprotic acid gives i = 1.06 in dilute water. On the simple dissociation model, what percentage of the acid is dissociated?
solution: B - 6% HA forms two ions on dissociation. The particle ratio is 1 + α, so α = 1.06 − 1 = 0.06, or 6%.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: An equal number of moles of non-electrolyte U and salt NaCl are dissolved separately in equal masses of water. If NaCl dissociates completely, what is the ratio of the measured freezing-point depressions, NaCl : U?
solution: A - 2 : 1 The initial molalities and solvent Kf are equal. NaCl has i = 2 and U has i = 1, so ΔTf is in the ratio 2 : 1.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1

question:

Q. Ethanol in water
2. Liquid in liquid
R. Zinc in copper (brass)

solution: C - P–3, Q–2, R–4, S–1 Hydrogen in palladium is gas-in-solid, ethanol in water is liquid-in-liquid, brass is solid-in-solid, and oxygen in nitrogen is gas-in-gas.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1

question:
Match the concentration term with its definition. The component named is X.

Column II

Q. Molality of X
2. Grams of X per 100 g of solution
R. Mole fraction of X
3. Moles of X per litre of solution
S. Mass percentage of X
4. Moles of X per kilogram of solvent
solution: A - P–3, Q–4, R–1, S–2 Molarity uses litres of solution, molality uses kilograms of solvent, mole fraction uses total moles, and mass percentage uses grams per 100 g of solution.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each pair of liquids with its characteristic behaviour in the standard NCERT
examples.
Column I
Column II
P. Benzene and toluene
1. Positive deviation from Raoult’s law
Q. Ethanol and acetone
2. Maximum-boiling azeotrope
R. Chloroform and acetone
3. Nearly ideal solution
S. Nitric acid and water at the azeotropic
composition
4. Negative deviation associated with
acetone–chloroform hydrogen bonding
solution: A - P–3, Q–1, R–4, S–2 Benzene–toluene is nearly ideal, ethanol–acetone shows positive deviation, acetone–chloroform hydrogen bonding gives negative deviation, and nitric acid–water forms a maximum-boiling azeotrope.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each colligative property with its expression for an ideal dilute solution. Here m is
molality, C is molarity, and x2 is the solute mole fraction. The solute is a non-volatile
non-electrolyte.
Column I
Column II
P. Relative lowering of vapour pressure
1. Kf × m
Q. Boiling-point elevation
2. C × R × T
R. Freezing-point depression
3. x2
S. Osmotic pressure
4. Kb × m
solution: C - P–3, Q–4, R–1, S–2 The equations are Δp/p° = x<sub>2</sub>, ΔTb = Kbm, ΔTf = Kfm and Π = CRT for the given non-electrolyte.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each practical situation with the principle involved.
Column I
Column II
P. Using a membrane and pressure to desalinate
water
1. Water leaves cells by osmosis
Q. Preserving fruit in a concentrated sugar syrup
2. Freezing-point depression
R. Adding ethylene glycol to car coolant in winter
3. Reverse osmosis
S. Determining a polymer’s molar mass at room
temperature
4. Osmotic-pressure measurement
solution: B - P–3, Q–1, R–2, S–4 Desalination uses reverse osmosis. Concentrated syrup draws water out of cells, glycol depresses freezing point, and osmotic pressure yields polymer molar mass at room temperature.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match the condition with the predicted initial net flow of water. The membrane passes
water only.
Column I
Column II
P. Pure water versus salt solution at equal pressures
1. Water leaves the cell.
Q. Isotonic solutions at equal pressures
2. Water enters the salt solution from the pure-water
side.
R. Salt-solution side pressurised above the osmotic
pressure against pure water
3. Water moves from the salt solution towards the
pure-water side.
S. Plant cell surrounded by a hypertonic solution at
equal initial pressure
4. No net water flow.
solution: D - P–2, Q–4, R–3, S–1 Water enters the unpressurised salt solution, has zero net flow between isotonic solutions, leaves the pressurised salt solution in reverse osmosis, and exits a plant cell in a hypertonic medium.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each solute behaviour with its van’t Hoff factor i. Assume ideal behaviour.
Column I
Column II
P. Complete dissociation of Na2SO4
1. 1.50
Q. 50% association of U into tetramers
2. 0.625
R. 35% dissociation of KCl
3. 3.00
S. 25% dissociation of MgCl2
4. 1.35
solution: C - P–3, Q–2, R–4, S–1 Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> gives 3 particles. Tetramerisation gives 0.50 + 0.50/4 = 0.625. KCl gives 1 + 0.35 = 1.35 and MgCl<sub>2</sub> gives 1 + 2(0.25) = 1.50.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each observed result with the degree of association or dissociation predicted by
the stated model.
Column I
Column II
P. U forms dimers, i = 0.75
1. 20% dissociation
Q. V forms trimers, i = 0.60
2. 50% association
R. AB gives two ions, i = 1.20
3. 60% dissociation
S. AB2 gives three ions, i = 2.20
4. 60% association
solution: B - P–2, Q–4, R–1, S–3 For association i = 1 − α(1 − 1/n), giving 50% and 60%. For dissociation i = 1 + α(n − 1), giving 20% and 60%.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Mass percentage is unchanged when the temperature of a sealed solution changes without evaporation or reaction. Reason (R) Mass percentage is a ratio of masses and neither mass changes under these conditions.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Mass percentage is a ratio of conserved masses in this sealed system, so a volume change caused by temperature cannot change it.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) An aqueous solution of glucose conducts electricity much less effectively than a comparable aqueous solution of NaCl. Reason (R) Glucose and sodium chloride can both be dissolved in water.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true, but solubility alone does not explain conductivity. NaCl produces mobile ions in water whereas dissolved glucose remains molecular.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A saturated solution in contact with undissolved solute has a constant dissolved concentration at equilibrium. Reason (R) At equilibrium, dissolution and crystallisation both stop.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true at fixed temperature. R is false because dissolution and crystallisation continue at equal rates in a dynamic equilibrium.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) At the same partial pressure, a gas with a larger Henry constant is more soluble in the same solvent. Reason (R) At fixed temperature, its dissolved mole fraction is given by x = p/KH.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false. R gives x = p/KH, so at fixed p the gas with the larger KH is less soluble.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) An ideal mixture shows zero enthalpy change of mixing. Reason (R) The total vapour pressure of an ideal binary mixture is linear in liquid mole fraction at fixed temperature.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are ideal-solution properties. Linear pressure follows from Raoult’s law, while zero mixing enthalpy reflects comparable unlike and like interactions.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A vapour over an ideal mixture has the same composition as its liquid if the two pure vapour pressures are equal at that temperature. Reason (R) Each component then contributes a partial pressure proportional to its liquid mole fraction with the same proportionality constant.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. If p°(A) = p°(B) = p°, then p(total) = p° and y(A) = x(A)p°/p° = x(A). The same follows for B.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) At the same molality in the same solvent, two non-electrolyte solutes must give different boiling-point elevations if their molar masses differ. Reason (R) The elevation depends on solute-particle molality for an ideal dilute solution.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false. R is true because ΔTb = Kbm for a non-electrolyte, so equal molality in the same solvent gives equal elevation.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) An ideal dilute solution of a non-electrolyte has twice the osmotic pressure when its molarity is doubled at fixed temperature. Reason (R) The osmotic pressure of such a solution is proportional to the square of its molarity.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true. R is false since Π = CRT is proportional to C, so doubling C doubles Π.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) An observed van’t Hoff factor below one is consistent with solute association. Reason (R) Osmotic pressure is measurable at room temperature.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. Association lowers the number of independent solute particles, which explains i < 1. The measurement temperature of osmotic pressure does not explain it.

heading: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 1 Solutions Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Dissociation can make a molar mass calculated from a colligative property smaller than the normal molar mass. Reason (R) Dissociation increases the effective number of solute particles, increasing the colligative effect for a given amount of solute.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Dissociation makes i > 1. Ignoring it interprets a greater colligative effect as more solute moles and thus gives M(apparent) = M(normal)/i.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In the operating cell Mg ∣ Mg<sup>2+</sup> ∣∣ Ag<sup>+</sup> ∣ Ag, electrons travel through the wire in which direction?
solution: C - Mg to Ag Mg is oxidised to Mg<sup>2+</sup> at the anode. Ag<sup>+</sup> is reduced to Ag at the cathode, so electrons travel through the wire from Mg to Ag.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In a working Zn–Cu cell with a KNO<sub>3</sub> bridge, which ion migrates towards the zinc compartment?
solution: A - NO<sub>3</sub><sup>-</sup> Zn<sup>2+</sup> accumulates at the anode as Zn oxidises. Nitrate ions enter that compartment to offset the buildup of positive charge.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: E°(Fe<sup>2+</sup>/Fe) = −0.44 V and E°(Cu<sup>2+</sup>/Cu) = +0.34 V. What is E° for spontaneous iron oxidation by Cu<sup>2+</sup>?
solution: D - 0.78 V Cu<sup>2+</sup> is reduced and Fe is oxidised. Using reduction potentials, E° = +0.34 − (−0.44) = +0.78 V.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which metal can reduce Zn<sup>2+</sup> under standard conditions? E°(Zn<sup>2+</sup>/Zn) = −0.76 V.
solution: D - Mg, E° = −2.37 V Mg has the more negative reduction potential. Pairing Mg oxidation with Zn<sup>2+</sup> reduction gives E° = −0.76 − (−2.37) = +1.61 V.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In Zn + Cu<sup>2+</sup> → Zn<sup>2+</sup> + Cu, how does increasing [Cu<sup>2+</sup>] alone affect the EMF at fixed temperature?
options: Makes it zero at any concentration
solution: B - Increases it Q = a(Zn<sup>2+</sup>)/a(Cu<sup>2+</sup>). Increasing Cu<sup>2+</sup> lowers Q, so the subtraction term in E = E° − (RT/nF)ln Q becomes smaller and E increases.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: For a two-electron reaction at 298 K, E° = 0.40 V and Q = 10<sup>2</sup>. Use 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V. What is E?

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A cell has E° = 0.118 V at 298 K and n = 1. Using 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V, find K.
solution: C - 10<sup>2</sup> At equilibrium E = 0 and Q = K, so log K = nE°/0.059 = 0.118/0.059 = 2. Thus K = 100.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: For n = 2 and E° = 0.80 V, find ΔG° using F = 96 500 C mol<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which statements hold when a reversible cell reaction reaches equilibrium?
options: Q = K and E = E° always
solution: A - Q = K and E = 0 At equilibrium the reaction quotient has reached K and ΔG = 0. The relation ΔG = −nFE then gives E = 0.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why is the pure metal absent from the Nernst reaction quotient in a typical metal–metal-ion cell?
options: Activity of dissolved ions, taken as 1
Activity of a pure solid, taken as 1
solution: C - Activity of a pure solid, taken as 1 A pure solid has unit activity. Including that factor in the quotient would simply multiply or divide by one.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: The resistance of an electrolyte in the same conductivity cell rises fourfold. What happens to conductivity?
solution: B - Falls to one-fourth Conductivity equals the cell constant divided by resistance. With fixed geometry, a fourfold resistance gives one-fourth the conductivity.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A cell with constant 0.80 cm<sup>-1</sup> contains a solution of conductance 0.020 S. Find κ.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: κ = 0.0015 S cm<sup>-1</sup> at 0.010 M. Find Λm.
solution: C - 150 S cm<sup>2</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup> Λm = 1000κ/c = 1000 × 0.0015/0.010 = 150 S cm<sup>2</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup> when c is in mol L<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which geometrical change doubles the cell constant ℓ/A?
solution: A - Doubling electrode separation alone The cell constant is ℓ/A. Doubling ℓ at fixed A doubles ℓ/A.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which pair of trends usually occurs on diluting an electrolyte?
solution: A - κ decreases and Λm increases Dilution usually lowers the number of ions per unit volume and hence κ. Interionic interactions decrease and weak electrolytes ionise more, so Λm increases.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which plot can be extrapolated approximately linearly to determine Λ°m for a strong electrolyte at low concentration?
solution: B - Λm versus √c At low concentration a strong electrolyte follows Λm ≈ Λ°m − A√c. The intercept of Λm against √c is Λ°m.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which combination gives Λ°m(CH<sub>3</sub>COOH)?
solution: D - Λ°m(HCl) + Λ°m(CH<sub>3</sub>COONa) − Λ°m(NaCl) Kohlrausch’s law allows ionic sums. Add HCl and CH<sub>3</sub>COONa, then subtract NaCl to cancel Na<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup> and retain H<sup>+</sup> and acetate.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A weak electrolyte has Λm = 12 and Λ°m = 300 S cm<sup>2</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup>. Estimate its degree of dissociation.
solution: C - 0.040 The weak-electrolyte estimate is α = Λm/Λ°m = 12/300 = 0.040, or 4.0%.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: How much charge is needed to discharge 0.25 mol of Al<sup>3+</sup> completely?
solution: D - 0.75 F Al<sup>3+</sup> + 3e<sup>-</sup> → Al. The charge for 0.25 mol is 3 × 0.25 = 0.75 faraday, or approximately 72 375 C.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A 2.00 A current passes for 965 s. How many moles of electrons pass? F = 96 500 C mol<sup>-1</sup>.
solution: B - 0.0200 mol Q = It = 2.00 × 965 = 1930 C. The amount of electrons is 1930/96 500 = 0.0200 mol.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: How much Ag is deposited by 0.10 F from AgNO<sub>3</sub> at 100% efficiency? M(Ag) = 108 g mol<sup>-1</sup>.
solution: B - 10.8 g Ag<sup>+</sup> needs one electron per ion, so 0.10 F deposits 0.10 mol of Ag. The mass is 0.10 × 108 = 10.8 g.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: The same charge deposits Cu from Cu<sup>2+</sup> and Ag from Ag<sup>+</sup>. What is the mole ratio Ag : Cu?
solution: D - 2 : 1 Ag<sup>+</sup> requires one electron per ion and Cu<sup>2+</sup> requires two. Equal charge deposits twice as many moles of Ag as Cu.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which species forms at the anode during electrolysis of molten NaCl?
solution: B - Cl<sub>2</sub> At the anode chloride is oxidised: 2Cl<sup>-</sup> → Cl<sub>2</sub> + 2e<sup>-</sup>. Sodium ions are reduced at the cathode.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which gas is released at the cathode during electrolysis of concentrated aqueous NaCl with inert electrodes?
solution: A - H<sub>2</sub> In aqueous brine, water is reduced at the cathode: 2H<sub>2</sub>O + 2e<sup>-</sup> → H<sub>2</sub> + 2OH<sup>-</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which solid accumulates at both plates of a lead storage battery during discharge?
solution: D - PbSO<sub>4</sub> Pb at the negative plate and PbO<sub>2</sub> at the positive plate both become PbSO<sub>4</sub> during discharge, consuming sulfuric acid.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What happens to sulfuric acid concentration during charging of a lead storage battery?
solution: B - It rises. Charging reverses the discharge reaction. PbSO<sub>4</sub> is converted back into the active plate materials and sulfuric acid is regenerated.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which cell is designed for repeated charging and discharging?
solution: C - Lead storage battery The lead storage battery is a secondary cell. Applying an external current reverses its discharge reaction so it can be used repeatedly.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell, which reactant is supplied to the electrode at which oxidation occurs?
solution: D - H<sub>2</sub> at the anode Hydrogen is the fuel and loses electrons at the anode. Oxygen accepts electrons at the cathode.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In aerated neutral water, what is the usual cathodic product when O<sub>2</sub> is reduced during iron corrosion?
solution: A - OH<sup>-</sup> The neutral-water cathodic half-reaction is O<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O + 4e<sup>-</sup> → 4OH<sup>-</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Connecting Mg to iron suppresses rusting because Mg does what?
options: Acts as a passive layer of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>
Increases the rate of iron oxidation
solution: C - Oxidises preferentially Mg oxidises preferentially to Mg<sup>2+</sup>. It supplies electrons to the iron, acting as a sacrificial anode.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each cell symbol with its meaning.
Column I
Column II
P. Single vertical line
1. Inert conducting electrode
Q. Double vertical line
2. Phase boundary
R. Pt(s) beside H2
3. Salt bridge or liquid junction
S. Cell notation from left to right
4. Anode to cathode for the stated galvanic reaction
solution: D - P–2, Q–3, R–1, S–4 A single line shows a phase boundary, a double line a liquid junction, Pt is an inert conductor, and conventional galvanic notation places the anode first.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each numerical condition with E for a cell having E° = 0.50 V, n = 2 at 298 K. Use
2.303RT/F = 0.059 V.
Column I
Column II
P. Q = 1
1. 0.559 V
Q. Q = 102
2. 0.441 V
R. Q = 10-2
3. 0.382 V
S. Q = 104
4. 0.500 V
solution: D - P–4, Q–2, R–1, S–3 Substitute in E = 0.50 − (0.059/2)log Q. For the four Q values the potentials are 0.500, 0.441, 0.559 and 0.382 V.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each quantity with its relation.
Column I
Column II
P. Conductance G
1. ℓ/A
Q. Conductivity κ
2. 1/R
R. Cell constant
3. 1000κ/c for c in mol L-1
S. Molar conductivity in S cm2 mol-1
4. G × cell constant
solution: B - P–2, Q–4, R–1, S–3 G = 1/R, κ = Gℓ/A, cell constant = ℓ/A, and Λm = 1000κ/c for c in mol L<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each quantity with a valid unit.
Column I
Column II
P. Conductivity
1. Ω
Q. Molar conductivity
2. S cm-1
R. Resistance
3. cm-1
S. Cell constant
4. S cm2 mol-1
solution: A - P–2, Q–4, R–1, S–3 Conductivity is in S cm<sup>-1</sup>, molar conductivity in S cm<sup>2</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup>, resistance in Ω, and ℓ/A in cm<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each ion with charge needed to deposit 1 mol of the metal.
Column I
Column II
P. Ag+
1. 4F
Q. Cu2+
2. F
R. Al3+
3. 3F
S. Sn4+
4. 2F
solution: C - P–2, Q–4, R–3, S–1 One mole of metal receives the number of electron moles given by the ionic charge: 1 for Ag<sup>+</sup>, 2 for Cu<sup>2+</sup>, 3 for Al<sup>3+</sup> and 4 for Sn<sup>4+</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each electrode process with its product.
Column I
Column II
P. Cathode of molten NaCl electrolysis
1. Cl2
Q. Anode of molten NaCl electrolysis
2. O2
R. Cathode of brine electrolysis
3. Na
S. Inert anode during electrolysis of acidified water
4. H2
solution: A - P–3, Q–1, R–4, S–2 Molten NaCl gives Na at the cathode and Cl<sub>2</sub> at the anode. Aqueous brine gives H<sub>2</sub> at the cathode, and acidified water gives O<sub>2</sub> at the inert anode.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each electrochemical device with its identifying feature.
Column I
Column II
P. Lead storage battery
1. Pb and PbO2 plates
Q. Leclanché dry cell
2. HgO cathode active material
R. Mercury cell
3. Zinc container and MnO2 depolariser
S. Hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell
4. Continuous supply of reactant gases
solution: B - P–1, Q–3, R–2, S–4 The lead battery has Pb/PbO<sub>2</sub> plates. The Leclanché cell uses zinc and MnO<sub>2</sub>, the mercury cell uses HgO, and a fuel cell uses externally supplied gases.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each fuel-cell or corrosion process to its equation.
Column I
Column II
P. H2 oxidation in alkaline medium
1. H2 + 2OH- → 2H2O + 2e-
Q. O2 reduction in alkaline medium
2. Fe2+ + 2OH- → Fe(OH)2
R. Anodic dissolution of iron
3. O2 + 2H2O + 4e- → 4OH-
S. Precipitation of ferrous hydroxide
4. Fe → Fe2+ + 2e-
solution: B - P–1, Q–3, R–4, S–2 H<sub>2</sub> loses electrons in alkaline medium, while O<sub>2</sub> gains electrons to give OH<sup>-</sup>. Iron loses electrons to Fe<sup>2+</sup>, which combines with OH<sup>-</sup> to precipitate Fe(OH)<sub>2</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match the condition with its thermodynamic implication for the reaction as written.
Column I
Column II
P. E° > 0
1. K > 1
Q. E° < 0
2. ΔG° > 0
R. E° = 0=K
3. ΔG < 0 under those conditions
S. E > 0 under actual conditions
4. 1
solution: A - P–1, Q–2, R–4, S–3 E° > 0 gives K > 1, and E° < 0 gives ΔG° > 0. For row R, read “E° = 0” on the left and “K = 1” on the right. E > 0 gives ΔG < 0 under the stated conditions.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each conductivity observation with its explanation.
Column I
Column II
P. Λm of weak electrolyte rises steeply on dilution
1. Ionisation increases substantially
Q. Conductivity usually falls on dilution
2. Kohlrausch’s law
R. Limiting ionic contributions add
3. Fewer charge carriers per unit volume
S. Alternating current used in conductivity
measurement
4. Reduced electrode polarisation
solution: C - P–1, Q–3, R–2, S–4 Weak-electrolyte ionisation rises upon dilution. Ions per unit volume fall, ionic contributions add at infinite dilution, and alternating current reduces electrode polarisation.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) E°cell remains unchanged when the balanced reaction is multiplied by two. Reason (R) Cell potential is an extensive property.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Doubling the reaction doubles n and ΔG°, leaving −ΔG°/(nF) unchanged. Potential is intensive.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Zn is the anode in an operating Daniell cell. Reason (R) Zn is oxidised to Zn<sup>2+</sup> in the spontaneous cell reaction.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Zn loses electrons to form Zn<sup>2+</sup>, and oxidation defines the anode.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A salt bridge helps maintain electrical neutrality in each half-cell. Reason (R) Electrons travel through the salt bridge from anode to cathode.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Salt-bridge ions move to preserve neutrality. Electrons travel in the external wire.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Depositing one mole of Al requires three faradays from Al<sup>3+</sup>. Reason (R) Each Al<sup>3+</sup> ion gains three electrons.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. One mole of Al<sup>3+</sup> accepts 3 mol of electrons, so deposition requires 3 F.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A fuel cell can keep operating while reactants are supplied. Reason (R) A fuel cell stores all reactants permanently inside its electrodes.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Fuel flows in from outside and the cell operates while reactants are supplied and products can be removed.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A Mg block can protect iron against corrosion. Reason (R) Mg oxidises more readily than iron and acts as a sacrificial anode.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Mg has the more negative reduction potential and oxidises in preference to Fe.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A standard hydrogen electrode is assigned zero standard potential. Reason (R) Its inert conductor is platinum.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. The zero potential of the standard hydrogen electrode is assigned by convention. Platinum supplies an inert conducting surface.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Lead storage batteries are secondary cells. Reason (R) The electrolyte in a lead storage battery contains sulfuric acid.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. The battery is secondary because discharge can be reversed by charging. Sulfuric acid is its electrolyte.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) The EMF at equilibrium is always equal to the standard EMF. Reason (R) The reaction quotient equals K at equilibrium.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. At Q = K the equilibrium EMF is zero, while E° is defined for standard states and need not be zero.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Molar conductivity of a weak electrolyte decreases on dilution. Reason (R) Dilution increases the degree of dissociation of a weak electrolyte.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Dilution increases the degree of dissociation and therefore increases molar conductivity.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In 2A → B, [A] decreases by 0.24 M in 12 s. What is the average reaction rate?
solution: A - 0.010 M s<sup>-1</sup> The disappearance rate of A is 0.24/12 = 0.020 M s<sup>-1</sup>. Divide by the coefficient 2 to obtain the reaction rate, 0.010 M s<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: For A → 3B, B appears at 0.12 M s<sup>-1</sup>. How fast is A consumed?
solution: C - 0.040 M s<sup>-1</sup> Three moles of B appear for every mole of A consumed. The disappearance rate of A is 0.12/3 = 0.040 M s<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which quantity gives the instantaneous rate of disappearance of A?
options: Magnitude of tangent slope on an [A] versus t curve
Slope joining t = 0 and the final point
solution: C - Magnitude of tangent slope on an [A] versus t curve At the required instant the tangent gives d[A]/dt. Since [A] falls, the disappearance rate is the positive magnitude −d[A]/dt.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A and B react with rate k[A]<sup>2</sup>[B]. If [A] is halved and [B] is doubled, what happens to rate?
solution: D - Becomes half The new rate divided by the old is (1/2)<sup>2</sup> × 2 = 1/2.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Doubling [A] quadruples the rate. Doubling [B] separately leaves it unchanged. What is the rate law?
solution: A - k[A]<sup>2</sup> Since 2<sup>2</sup> = 4, the exponent of A is 2. B has exponent zero because doubling its concentration has no effect, so r = k[A]<sup>2</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: For r = k[A]1/2[B], what is overall order?
solution: A - 1.5 Add the exponents in the rate law: 1/2 + 1 = 1.5.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which unit of k is consistent with a second-order rate law in mol L<sup>-1</sup> and seconds?
solution: B - L mol<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup> Divide rate units (mol L<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>) by concentration squared (mol<sup>2</sup> L<sup>-2</sup>). The result is L mol<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A reaction is zero order in A over a stated range. What happens on doubling [A] alone within that range?
solution: A - No rate change Over that range [A] enters the rate law as [A]<sup>0</sup> = 1. Doubling [A] therefore leaves the rate unchanged.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What does molecularity count?
options: Number of steps in a mechanism
Reacting species in a single elementary step
Sum of empirical exponents for any reaction
solution: B - Reacting species in a single elementary step Molecularity counts the particles participating in one elementary step, so it is a positive integer.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which statement about order is valid?
options: It always equals the largest stoichiometric coefficient.
It is independent of the experimentally observed rate law.
It always equals molecularity of the overall reaction.
solution: B - It may be fractional. Reaction order is the sum of the experimentally determined rate-law exponents. These exponents may be fractional.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: For a zero-order reaction, [A]<sub>0</sub> = 0.60 M and k = 0.025 M min<sup>-1</sup>. Find [A] after 8 min.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: For a zero-order decay, [A] halves in 20 min from 0.80 M. What is k?
solution: B - 0.020 M min<sup>-1</sup> A loss of 0.40 M in 20 min gives k = 0.40/20 = 0.020 M min<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: If the initial concentration of a zero-order reactant is tripled at the same k, what happens to its half-life?
solution: D - It triples. The zero-order relation t1/2 = [A]<sub>0</sub>/(2k) makes the half-life directly proportional to [A]<sub>0</sub> at fixed k.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which linear plot with a negative slope describes a first-order decay?
solution: C - ln[A] versus t The integrated first-order law is ln[A] = ln[A]<sub>0</sub> − kt. A graph of ln[A] against t is linear with slope −k.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: The slope of ln[A] versus t is −0.031 s<sup>-1</sup>. What is k?
solution: D - 0.031 s<sup>-1</sup> For the integrated first-order law the slope is −k. Therefore k = 0.031 s<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A first-order process has half-life 8 min. What percentage remains after 24 min?
solution: A - 12.5% Twenty-four minutes is three half-lives, leaving (1/2)<sup>3</sup> = 1/8 of the initial amount, or 12.5%.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A first-order reaction reaches 75% completion in 36 min. Find its half-life.
solution: A - 18 min At 75% completion, 25% remains. This is two halvings (1/2 × 1/2), so one half-life takes 36/2 = 18 min.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A first-order k is 0.03465 min<sup>-1</sup>. With ln 2 = 0.693, find the half-life.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which initial concentration change leaves a first-order half-life unchanged at fixed temperature?
options: Raising temperature enough to double k
solution: A - Doubling the starting concentration For first-order kinetics t1/2 = ln 2/k. Doubling the starting concentration does not change k at fixed temperature under the given conditions.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: For A(g) → 2B(g), pure A initially exerts 0.50 atm. Total pressure at time t is 0.80 atm at fixed T and V. Find partial pressure of A.
solution: D - 0.20 atm Let x be the pressure equivalent of A consumed. Then p(A) = 0.50 − x, p(B) = 2x, and 0.80 = 0.50 + x. Thus x = 0.30 atm and p(A) = 0.20 atm.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which change often makes acid-catalysed ester hydrolysis pseudo-first order in ester?
options: Water kept at half the ester concentration
Temperature raised while all concentrations fluctuate
solution: C - Water kept in large excess With water in large excess, its concentration stays nearly constant. Its rate-law factor is included in the observed rate constant, leaving first-order dependence on ester.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which factor is represented by A in k = A exp(−Ea/RT)?
solution: C - Pre-exponential factor A is the pre-exponential or frequency factor. It multiplies the temperature-dependent Arrhenius exponential.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In a plot of log<sub>10</sub>k versus 1/T, what is the slope?
solution: D - −Eₐ/(2.303R) Taking common logarithms gives log k = log A − (Eₐ/2.303R)(1/T). The coefficient of 1/T is the slope.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: For an Arrhenius plot of ln k versus 1/T, slope = −4000 K. Find Ea with R = 8.31 J mol<sup>-1</sup> K<sup>-1</sup>.
solution: C - 33.2 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup> For a natural-log plot, slope = −Eₐ/R. Thus Eₐ = 4000 × 8.31 = 33 240 J mol<sup>-1</sup>, or 33.2 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which process increases k when a catalyst is added at fixed T?
options: The total collision frequency becomes zero.
An alternative path with lower activation energy becomes available.
solution: B - An alternative path with lower activation energy becomes available. A catalyst makes a pathway with a lower activation barrier available. This increases the rate constant at the given temperature.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why can a moderate temperature rise significantly increase reaction rate?
options: A larger fraction of molecules exceeds the activation barrier.
solution: C - A larger fraction of molecules exceeds the activation barrier. At higher temperature the fraction of molecules with energy at or above Eₐ grows, increasing the fraction of effective encounters.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What distinguishes an effective collision in simple collision theory?
options: Identical masses of the colliding molecules
solution: B - Adequate energy and suitable orientation An effective collision needs sufficient energy to overcome the activation barrier and a geometry that allows the necessary bonds to change.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: When volume of a closed gas vessel is halved at fixed T, concentration of A doubles. If rate = k[A]<sup>3</sup>, what is the new rate?
solution: B - 8 times With the same amount of A in half the volume, [A] doubles. For a cubic rate law this multiplies the rate by 2<sup>3</sup> = 8.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A reaction has k = 0.10 M s<sup>-1</sup> and its rate stays 0.10 M s<sup>-1</sup> over a concentration range. What is its order in that range?
solution: C - Zero The rate is constant and equals k, whose units are concentration per time. That is the zero-order form r = k.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A first-order reactant falls to 20% of its initial amount in time t. Which expression gives kt?
solution: C - ln 5 kt = ln([A]<sub>0</sub>/[A]) = ln(1/0.20) = ln 5.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each reaction with the coefficient relating reaction rate to disappearance rate of
A.
Column I
Column II
P. A → B
1. 1/2
Q. 2A → B
2. 1
R. 3A → 2B
3. 1/4
S. 4A → B
4. 1/3
solution: B - P–2, Q–1, R–4, S–3 Normalise −d[A]/dt by the coefficient of A. The four factors for coefficients 1, 2, 3 and 4 are 1, 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each order with the units of k when rate is in mol L-1 s-1.
Column I
Column II
P. Zero
1. L mol-1 s-1
Q. First
2. mol L-1 s-1
R. Second
3. s-1
S. Third
4. L2 mol-2 s-1
solution: D - P–2, Q–3, R–1, S–4 For order n use units [concentration]^(1−n) × [time]<sup>-1</sup>. Substitution for n = 0, 1, 2 and 3 gives the listed four matches.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each rate law with its overall order.
Column I
Column II
P. k[A]3
1. 2
Q. k[A]1/2
2. 1.5
R. k[A][B]
3. 0.5
S. k[A]1/2[B]
4. 3
solution: C - P–4, Q–3, R–1, S–2 Adding the concentration exponents gives 3, 0.5, 1 + 1 = 2, and 0.5 + 1 = 1.5, respectively.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each first-order time with the unreacted fraction.
Column I
Column II
P. One half-life
1. 1/8
Q. Two half-lives
2. 1/2
R. Three half-lives
3. 1/4
S. Four half-lives
4. 1/16
solution: A - P–2, Q–3, R–1, S–4 After j half-lives, the unreacted fraction is (1/2)<sup>j</sup>. For j = 1 to 4 the values are 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 and 1/16.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each zero-order quantity with its expression.
Column I
Column II
P. Concentration at time t
1. [A]0/(2k)
Q. Half-life
2. [A]0 − kt
R. Time to exhaustion
3. [A]0/k
S. Rate of disappearance before exhaustion
4. k
solution: D - P–2, Q–1, R–3, S–4 The integrated law is [A]<sub>0</sub> − kt. Setting it equal to [A]<sub>0</sub>/2 or zero gives [A]<sub>0</sub>/(2k) or [A]<sub>0</sub>/k. The disappearance rate is k.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each plot feature for a first-order reaction with the expression.
Column I
Column II
P. Slope of ln[A] versus t
1. −k
Q. Intercept of ln[A] versus t
2. ln[A]0
R. Half-life
3. ln 2/k
S. Rate at initial instant
4. k[A]0
solution: D - P–1, Q–2, R–3, S–4 Use ln[A] = ln[A]<sub>0</sub> − kt for slope and intercept. Replacing [A] with [A]<sub>0</sub>/2 gives half-life ln 2/k, and r(0) = k[A]<sub>0</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each Arrhenius feature with its expression.
Column I
Column II
P. Slope of ln k versus 1/T
1. ln A
Q. Slope of log10k versus 1/T
2. −Ea/R
R. Intercept of ln k versus 1/T
3. exp(−Ea/RT)
S. Factor multiplying A in k
4. −Ea/(2.303R)
solution: A - P–2, Q–4, R–1, S–3 Natural logarithms give slope −Eₐ/R and intercept ln A. Common logarithms divide the slope by 2.303. The factor multiplying A in k is exp(−Eₐ/RT).

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each observed effect with its likely explanation.
Column I
Column II
P. Rate constant rises on heating
1. Greater energetic fraction
Q. Water in large excess
2. Lower activation barrier
R. Catalysed path speeds approach to equilibrium
3. Pseudo-first-order treatment
S. Doubling [A] quadruples rate at fixed [B]
4. Second order with respect to A
solution: D - P–1, Q–3, R–2, S–4 Heating increases the energetic fraction, excess water makes its factor effectively constant, catalysis lowers the barrier, and the rate factor of four corresponds to exponent 2.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each exponent of A with the rate factor when [A] doubles and all other
concentrations stay fixed.
Column I
Column II
P. 0
1. 1
Q. 1
2. 2
R. 2
3. 4
S. 3
4. 8
solution: A - P–1, Q–2, R–3, S–4 For a rate term [A]<sup>n</sup> the multiplier is 2<sup>n</sup>. The four exponents give multipliers 1, 2, 4 and 8.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each first-order conversion with the corresponding remaining concentration.
Column I
Column II
P. 25% completion
1. 0.10[A]0
Q. 50% completion
2. 0.20[A]0
R. 80% completion
3. 0.50[A]0
S. 90% completion
4. 0.75[A]0
solution: B - P–4, Q–3, R–2, S–1 Subtract the completion fraction from one. The remaining fractions are 0.75, 0.50, 0.20 and 0.10, each multiplied by [A]<sub>0</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A rate law can have a fractional exponent. Reason (R) Molecularity can be fractional for an elementary step.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true because measured rate exponents may be fractional. R is false because molecularity counts a whole number of reacting particles.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Molecularity is defined for an elementary step. Reason (R) The overall balanced equation always establishes the experimental reaction order.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true. R is false because an overall stoichiometric equation can represent several elementary steps and need not give the observed rate law.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) All collisions with adequate energy necessarily lead to product. Reason (R) Reactant orientation can affect whether a collision is effective.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Sufficient energy alone is incomplete as a criterion because the reactants must also collide with suitable orientation.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A first-order rate constant has unit s<sup>-1</sup> when time is in seconds. Reason (R) A first-order process takes equal intervals for successive halvings at fixed temperature.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. The units follow by dividing the rate units by concentration. Equal successive half-lives follow separately from t1/2 = ln 2/k.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) At 75% completion a first-order reactant has undergone two half-lives. Reason (R) One-quarter remaining equals (1/2)<sup>2</sup>.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. At 75% completion 25% remains, which is (1/2)<sup>2</sup> and therefore corresponds to two half-lives.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Hydrolysis can appear first order in ester when water is in large excess. Reason (R) Water concentration is then approximately constant and can be included in the observed rate constant.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. A nearly constant water concentration can be absorbed into the observed rate constant so the change in rate follows the ester concentration.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Catalysing a reversible reaction changes its equilibrium constant at fixed T. Reason (R) A catalyst provides a lower-barrier path for equilibration.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Catalysis provides a lower-barrier pathway for both directions, allowing equilibrium to be reached faster at the same equilibrium constant.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) An Arrhenius plot of ln k versus 1/T has a negative slope if Ea > 0. Reason (R) Its slope is +Ea/R.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Taking natural logarithms gives the negative slope −Eₐ/R.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) The half-life of a zero-order reaction is proportional to [A]<sub>0</sub>. Reason (R) A constant amount of concentration is consumed per unit time.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Consuming a fixed concentration per unit time gives t1/2 = ([A]<sub>0</sub>/2)/k, directly proportional to [A]<sub>0</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 3 Chemical Kinetics Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) For a zero-order reaction, [A] versus t is a straight line before exhaustion. Reason (R) For a first-order reaction, ln[A] versus t is a straight line.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
