Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. The zero-order line comes from [A] = [A]<sub>0</sub> − kt, whereas the other line comes from the separate integrated first-order law.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which period contains the 3d transition series?
solution: D - 4 The first transition series fills the 3d subshell in period 4, beginning with Sc and ending with Zn as a d-block series.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which element belongs to the second transition series (4d)?
solution: A - Mo Mo is a period-5 d-block element and belongs to the 4d series. Its ground-state configuration is [Kr] 4d<sup>5</sup> 5s<sup>1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which subshell is progressively filled in the actinoids?
solution: D - 5f The actinoid series involves progressive filling of 5f orbitals. The corresponding filling for lanthanoids is 4f.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which is the ground-state configuration of Mo (Z = 42)?
solution: C - [Kr] 4d<sup>5</sup> 5s<sup>1</sup> Mo has the observed configuration [Kr] 4d<sup>5</sup> 5s<sup>1</sup>. The near energies of 4d and 5s permit this configuration with a half-filled d subshell.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is removed first when gaseous Fe forms Fe<sup>2+</sup> from its ground-state atom?
solution: D - Two 4s electrons Neutral Fe is [Ar] 3d<sup>6</sup> 4s<sup>2</sup>. For gaseous Fe<sup>2+</sup> the two outer 4s electrons are removed, giving [Ar] 3d<sup>6</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why is Cd excluded from the transition elements under the incomplete d-subshell definition?
options: Cd and Cd<sup>2+</sup> both have filled d subshells.
Cd<sup>2+</sup> has one unpaired d electron.
solution: B - Cd and Cd<sup>2+</sup> both have filled d subshells. Cd is [Kr] 4d<sup>10</sup> 5s<sup>2</sup> and Cd<sup>2+</sup> is [Kr] 4d<sup>10</sup>. Neither has the incompletely filled d subshell required by the definition.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which free ion is expected to have four unpaired 3d electrons? Atomic numbers: Mn 25, Fe 26, Co 27, Ni 28.
solution: C - Fe<sup>2+</sup> Fe<sup>2+</sup> has 3d<sup>6</sup>. By Hund’s rule five orbitals first receive one electron each, then the sixth pairs, leaving four unpaired.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which free ion has spin-only magnetic moment √8 BM? Atomic numbers: Ti 22, Cr 24, Mn 25, Cu 29.
solution: D - Ti<sup>2+</sup> From μ = √[n(n + 2)] BM, √8 corresponds to n = 2. Ti<sup>2+</sup> is 3d<sup>2</sup> with two unpaired electrons by Hund’s rule.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which ion is normally colourless in aqueous solution on the basis of its d-electron configuration?
solution: C - Zn<sup>2+</sup> Zn<sup>2+</sup> is 3d<sup>10</sup>. Its filled d orbitals do not allow d–d excitation, so the ordinary aqueous ion is colourless.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which property makes transition metals useful in alloy formation?
options: Relatively similar atomic sizes within a series
Completely filled valence shells in every metal
solution: A - Relatively similar atomic sizes within a series Metals with similar atomic radii can substitute for one another in a crystal lattice, favouring alloy formation.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which small atom can occupy interstitial sites in a transition-metal lattice?
solution: D - Carbon Carbon is sufficiently small to occupy interstitial sites in many transition-metal lattices. Other representative small atoms include H and N.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which first-row metal is commonly used as catalyst in ammonia synthesis?
solution: A - Iron Finely divided iron is the conventional Haber-process catalyst for making ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In which compound is Mn in the +4 state?
solution: B - MnO<sub>2</sub> With each oxygen at −2, the two oxygens contribute −4. The neutral formula therefore requires manganese at +4.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the change in the chromium oxidation state when dichromate is reduced to Cr<sup>3+</sup>?
solution: C - +6 to +3 In Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub><sup>2-</sup>, 2x + 7(−2) = −2 gives x = +6. Formation of Cr<sup>3+</sup> reduces chromium to +3.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the colour of aqueous manganate ion, MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup>?
solution: A - Green The manganate ion, MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup>, is green in aqueous solution. Permanganate, MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup>, is purple.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product normally forms when permanganate is reduced by a suitable reductant in neutral water?
options: MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup> as the usual final product
solution: A - MnO<sub>2</sub> In neutral water the standard product is MnO<sub>2</sub>. Mn changes from +7 in MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup> to +4 in MnO<sub>2</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: How many moles of Fe<sup>2+</sup> can one mole of acidified MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup> oxidise to Fe<sup>3+</sup>?
solution: B - 5 MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup> + 8H<sup>+</sup> + 5e<sup>-</sup> → Mn<sup>2+</sup> + 4H<sub>2</sub>O. Each Fe<sup>2+</sup> supplies one electron, so five moles are oxidised.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is oxidised when acidified dichromate reacts with iodide?
solution: C - I<sup>-</sup> to I<sub>2</sub> Iodide loses electrons: 2I<sup>-</sup> → I<sub>2</sub> + 2e<sup>-</sup>. Acidified dichromate accepts electrons and is reduced to Cr<sup>3+</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which ions have the same number of d electrons? Atomic numbers: V 23, Cr 24, Mn 25, Fe 26.
solution: C - V<sup>3+</sup> and Cr<sup>4+</sup> V<sup>3+</sup> has two 3d electrons after removing 4s<sup>2</sup> and one 3d electron. Cr<sup>4+</sup> also has 3d<sup>2</sup> after removing 4s<sup>1</sup> and three 3d electrons.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why is aqueous Cu<sup>+</sup> prone to disproportionation in the absence of stabilising ligands?
options: Cu metal cannot form in water.
Hydration strongly favours Cu<sup>2+</sup> relative to Cu<sup>+</sup>.
Cu<sup>2+</sup> has no stabilisation in water.
Cu<sup>+</sup> has an unstable half-filled 3d subshell.
solution: B - Hydration strongly favours Cu<sup>2+</sup> relative to Cu<sup>+</sup>. In water, strong hydration stabilises Cu<sup>2+</sup>. Together with the redox energetics, it favours 2Cu<sup>+</sup> → Cu<sup>2+</sup> + Cu(s).

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which oxidation state is most common for lanthanoids?
solution: D - +3 Lanthanoids most often form +3 ions by losing the two outer 6s electrons along with one additional valence electron.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: For Eu<sup>2+</sup> (Z = 63), which configuration explains the relative stability of this ion?
solution: A - 4f<sup>7</sup> Eu<sup>2+</sup> has [Xe] 4f<sup>7</sup>. The half-filled 4f subshell contributes to the stability of the +2 state.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which lanthanoid commonly exhibits a +4 state with a noble-gas core and no 4f electrons?
solution: C - Ce Ce<sup>4+</sup> has the [Xe] configuration, with 4f<sup>0</sup>. This empty 4f subshell is characteristic of Ce in its +4 state.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why is the separation of adjacent lanthanoids challenging?
options: Their ionic radii change by unusually large amounts between neighbours.
Their ions have similar sizes and chemical properties.
Their most stable oxidation states alternate between +1 and +7.
solution: C - Their ions have similar sizes and chemical properties. Adjacent lanthanoid ions are commonly +3 and differ only modestly in radius. Their similar chemical behaviour makes separation difficult.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which pair is a consequence of the similarity of 4d and 5d element sizes after lanthanoid contraction?
solution: A - Nb and Ta Lanthanoid contraction reduces the size of 5d elements. Period-6 Ta is consequently close in size to its 4d congener Nb.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What accounts for the generally greater actinoid contraction?
options: A steady increase in 5f orbital shielding efficiency
solution: D - Poor shielding by 5f electrons The 5f electrons shield one another poorly. Increasing nuclear charge therefore draws the electron cloud inward across the actinoid series.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which common property distinguishes all actinoids as a group?
options: They all show only the +3 state.
They all occur in large natural abundances.
solution: B - They are radioactive. All actinoids have radioactive nuclei, including naturally occurring thorium and uranium.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which industrial use is associated with V<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>?
options: Primary fuel in a hydrogen fuel cell
Bleaching agent in the chlor-alkali process
solution: A - Catalyst in the Contact process Vanadium(V) oxide catalyses the oxidation of SO<sub>2</sub> to SO<sub>3</sub> in the Contact process for sulfuric acid manufacture.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What contributes to the high atomisation enthalpies of many transition metals?
options: A lack of interactions between metal atoms
Strong metallic bonding involving valence electrons
Complete removal of all d electrons in the solid
solution: C - Strong metallic bonding involving valence electrons Both ns and (n−1)d valence electrons can contribute to strong metallic bonding. A large energy is then needed to separate the atoms.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which description identifies the redox-active centre in permanganate before reduction to Mn<sup>2+</sup>?
solution: C - Manganese in oxidation state +7 For MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup>, x + 4(−2) = −1 gives x = +7. This manganese centre accepts electrons on reduction to Mn<sup>2+</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each transition series with the subshell being filled.
Column I
Column II
P. First
1. 4d
Q. Second
2. 5d
R. Third
3. 6d
S. Fourth
4. 3d
solution: D - P–4, Q–1, R–2, S–3 The d series are named for the subshells that fill progressively: 3d, 4d, 5d and 6d in sequence.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each ground-state atom with its configuration after the noble-gas core.
Column I
Column II
P. Cr (Z = 24)
1. 3d10 4s1
Q. Mn (Z = 25)
2. 3d5 4s1
R. Cu (Z = 29)
3. 3d5 4s2
S. Zn (Z = 30)
4. 3d10 4s2
solution: A - P–2, Q–3, R–1, S–4 Cr is 3d<sup>5</sup> 4s<sup>1</sup> and Cu is 3d<sup>10</sup> 4s<sup>1</sup>. Mn and Zn retain 4s<sup>2</sup> with 3d<sup>5</sup> and 3d<sup>10</sup>, respectively.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each free ion with its number of unpaired 3d electrons.
Column I
Column II
P. Sc3+
1. 1
Q. Ti3+
2. 0
R. V3+
3. 2
S. Mn2+
4. 5
solution: B - P–2, Q–1, R–3, S–4 The 3d electron counts are 0, 1, 2 and 5 for Sc<sup>3+</sup>, Ti<sup>3+</sup>, V<sup>3+</sup> and Mn<sup>2+</sup>. For these free ions, each electron occupies a different d orbital.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each complex ion with its common colour in aqueous solution.
Column I
Column II
P. CrO42-
1. Green
Q. Cr2O72-
2. Purple
R. MnO4-
3. Yellow
S. MnO42-
4. Orange
solution: B - P–3, Q–4, R–2, S–1 The characteristic colours are chromate yellow, dichromate orange, permanganate purple and manganate green.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each formula with the metal oxidation state.
Column I
Column II
P. V2O5
1. +6
Q. CrO42-
2. +5
R. MnO4-
3. +7
S. MnO2
4. +4
solution: D - P–2, Q–1, R–3, S–4 Assign oxygen −2 and balance the total charge. V<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>, CrO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup>, MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup> and MnO<sub>2</sub> give +5, +6, +7 and +4, respectively.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match the reductive process with the number of electrons accepted per ion shown.
Column I
Column II
P. MnO4- → Mn2+
1. 3
Q. Cr2O72- → 2Cr3+
2. 6
R. MnO4- → MnO2
3. 1
S. MnO4- → MnO42-
4. 5
solution: A - P–4, Q–2, R–1, S–3 Mn falls from +7 to +2, +4 or +6, so it gains 5, 3 or 1 electron respectively. Dichromate contains two Cr atoms, each gaining three electrons.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each material with a representative use.
Column I
Column II
P. Fe
1. Contact process catalyst
Q. V2O5
2. Low-neutron-absorption cladding material
R. KMnO4
3. Haber process catalyst
S. Zr
4. Oxidant in redox titrations
solution: B - P–3, Q–1, R–4, S–2 Fe catalyses ammonia synthesis, V<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub> catalyses the Contact process, KMnO<sub>4</sub> oxidises analytes in titrations, and Zr has low neutron absorption for cladding.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each lanthanoid ion with its 4f electron count. Atomic numbers: Ce 58, Eu 63, Gd
64, Lu 71.
Column I
Column II
P. Ce4+
1. 0
Q. Eu3+
2. 7
R. Gd3+
3. 14
S. Lu3+
4. 6
solution: D - P–1, Q–4, R–2, S–3 The configurations are Ce<sup>4+</sup> 4f<sup>0</sup>, Eu<sup>3+</sup> 4f<sup>6</sup>, Gd<sup>3+</sup> 4f<sup>7</sup> and Lu<sup>3+</sup> 4f<sup>14</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each observation with its main explanation.
Column I
Column II
P. Close atomic sizes of Zr and Hf
1. Comparable ns and (n−1)d energies
Q. Multiple oxidation states
2. Lanthanoid contraction
R. Paramagnetism of Mn2+
3. Unpaired electrons
S. Formation of transition-metal carbides
4. Small atoms occupy lattice interstices
solution: B - P–2, Q–1, R–3, S–4 Contraction explains Zr/Hf size similarity, near ns and d energies give several oxidation states, unpaired spins give paramagnetism, and small carbon atoms fit interstitial sites.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each free-ion unpaired electron count n with its spin-only magnetic moment.
Column I
Column II
P. n = 1
1. √3 BM
Q. n = 2
2. √24 BM
R. n = 4
3. √8 BM
S. n = 5
4. √35 BM
solution: B - P–1, Q–3, R–2, S–4 Substitute n = 1, 2, 4 and 5 into μ = √[n(n + 2)] BM to get √3, √8, √24 and √35 BM.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Sc<sup>3+</sup> is ordinarily paramagnetic due to 3d electrons. Reason (R) Sc<sup>3+</sup> has a 3d<sup>0</sup> configuration.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Sc<sup>3+</sup> is [Ar] 3d<sup>0</sup> and has no unpaired 3d electrons, so it is ordinarily diamagnetic.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Lanthanoids commonly form +3 ions. Reason (R) Lanthanoid contraction occurs across the series.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. The +3 state reflects ionisation and bonding energetics. The contraction follows from poor 4f shielding and does not explain the preference for +3.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Many aqueous transition-metal ions are coloured. Reason (R) In a suitable ligand field, some ions can absorb visible light in d–d transitions.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. For ions with suitable partially occupied d levels, visible light can promote d–d transitions, leaving a characteristic colour in the transmitted light.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Transition metals can form interstitial compounds. Reason (R) Only very large atoms fit into interstitial sites in metal lattices.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Interstitial sites can accommodate sufficiently small atoms such as C, H and N.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Zr and Hf have similar atomic radii. Reason (R) Lanthanoid contraction offsets much of the expected size increase down the group.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Poor 4f shielding contracts Hf sufficiently to offset much of the size increase normally expected from Zr to Hf.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Acidified permanganate can oxidise Fe<sup>2+</sup> to Fe<sup>3+</sup>. Reason (R) In this reaction the Mn in MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup> is oxidised from +7 to +2.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Fe<sup>2+</sup> is oxidised to Fe<sup>3+</sup> and Mn(VII) gains electrons, so its change to Mn(II) is reduction.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub><sup>2-</sup> is yellow in water. Reason (R) CrO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup> is yellow in water.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Dichromate is orange and chromate is yellow in water.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Cd is excluded from the transition elements by the incomplete d-subshell definition. Reason (R) Both Cd and its normal Cd<sup>2+</sup> ion have a filled 4d subshell.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Cd and Cd<sup>2+</sup> are 4d<sup>10</sup>, so the ordinary atom and ion do not meet the incomplete d-subshell criterion.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Mn<sup>2+</sup> has five unpaired electrons in its free-ion configuration. Reason (R) Permanganate is purple in water.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. Mn<sup>2+</sup> is 3d<sup>5</sup> and follows Hund’s rule, while the colour of permanganate concerns a different ion.

heading: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Actinoids commonly show variable oxidation states. Reason (R) Uranium is radioactive.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. Variable actinoid oxidation states are linked to similar valence orbital energies. Radioactivity concerns nuclear stability.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the coordination number of Pt in [Pt(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>]?
solution: A - 4 Each of the two NH<sub>3</sub> and two Cl<sup>-</sup> ligands donates one atom to Pt. Four donor atoms give coordination number 4.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the oxidation state of Cr in [Cr(C<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>]<sup>3-</sup>?
solution: B - +3 Each oxalato ligand carries −2. With complex charge −3, x + 3(−2) = −3 and x = +3.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which particle is a counter-ion in [Cu(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>4</sub>]SO<sub>4</sub>?
solution: D - SO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup> The positively charged coordination entity is [Cu(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2+</sup>. The sulfate outside the brackets balances its charge.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which formula represents a complex anion with a metal in oxidation state +2?
solution: C - [Fe(CN)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>4-</sup> For [Fe(CN)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>4-</sup>, x + 6(−1) = −4. Fe is therefore +2 and the coordination entity is an anion.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which ligand has six donor atoms and is usually hexadentate?
solution: B - EDTA<sup>4-</sup> EDTA<sup>4-</sup> usually binds through two nitrogen and four oxygen donor atoms. Six attachments to one central ion make it hexadentate.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: How many oxalato ligands supply six donor atoms if each binds bidentately?
solution: B - 3 Each oxalato ligand supplies two oxygen donors, so 6/2 = 3 ligands are required.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which feature of SCN<sup>-</sup> permits linkage isomerism?
options: It can bind through S or N.
It always binds through S and N simultaneously.
solution: A - It can bind through S or N. SCN<sup>-</sup> is ambidentate. One form binds through S and the other through N, producing different connectivity.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which is a homoleptic complex?
solution: C - [Fe(CN)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3-</sup> Homoleptic means all ligands are of one type. The six ligands in [Fe(CN)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3-</sup> are cyanido.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the IUPAC name of K<sub>4</sub>[Fe(CN)<sub>6</sub>]?
solution: A - Potassium hexacyanidoferrate(II) The anion contains six cyanido ligands and Fe in state +2. An anionic iron complex uses the name ferrate, with potassium named first.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which formula represents tetraamminedichloridocobalt(III) chloride?
solution: A - [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>4</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>]Cl Four neutral NH<sub>3</sub> and two chlorido ligands around Co<sup>3+</sup> give a +1 complex. One outer chloride is needed to balance it.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: How many moles of AgCl precipitate immediately per mole of [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>5</sub>Cl]Cl<sub>2</sub> with excess AgNO<sub>3</sub> when only outer-sphere chloride reacts?
solution: D - 2 Two Cl<sup>-</sup> ions are outside the coordination sphere and precipitate with Ag<sup>+</sup>. The inner chlorido ligand remains coordinated under the stated conditions.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In Werner’s terminology, the primary valency of cobalt in [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>6</sub>]Cl<sub>3</sub> is what?
solution: D - 3 Werner’s primary valency corresponds to oxidation state. Six neutral NH<sub>3</sub> ligands and three outer chlorides imply Co<sup>3+</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which type of isomerism relates [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>5</sub>(NO<sub>2</sub>)]<sup>2+</sup> and [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>5</sub>(ONO)]<sup>2+</sup>?
solution: A - Linkage Both groups are nitrite, but one attaches through N and the other through O. This donor-atom change is linkage isomerism.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which metal complex can give cis and trans forms in a square plane?
solution: C - [Pt(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>] The square plane can arrange the two Cl ligands next to one another or opposite each other, giving cis and trans forms.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which geometrical isomer of octahedral MA<sub>3</sub>B<sub>3</sub> has the three B ligands on one face?
solution: C - fac On one triangular face of an octahedron the three B ligands are mutually cis. This is the facial, or fac, isomer.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which complex is a standard example of optical isomerism without cis–trans isomerism?
solution: B - [Cr(en)<sub>3</sub>]<sup>3+</sup> Three identical bidentate en ligands wrap into two non-superimposable helical arrangements, Δ and Λ. There is no separate cis–trans arrangement for this formula.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which pair differs by interchange of ligands between complex cation and complex anion?
solution: D - [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>6</sub>][Cr(CN)<sub>6</sub>] and [Cr(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>6</sub>][Co(CN)<sub>6</sub>] Both salts have a complex cation and a complex anion. Swapping which metal is surrounded by NH<sub>3</sub> and which by CN<sup>-</sup> gives coordination isomers.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which geometry does VBT predict for [ZnCl<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2-</sup> with sp<sup>3</sup> hybridisation?
solution: C - Tetrahedral Four sp<sup>3</sup> hybrid orbitals point towards the corners of a tetrahedron. The four chlorido ligands occupy those directions.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which VBT hybridisation is associated with square-planar [Ni(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2-</sup>?
solution: B - dsp<sup>2</sup> CN<sup>-</sup> gives square-planar d<sup>8</sup> Ni(II). The VBT description uses one d, one s and two p orbitals, dsp<sup>2</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which pair contains only diamagnetic complexes? Atomic number of Ni = 28.
solution: D - [Ni(CO)<sub>4</sub>] and [Ni(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2-</sup> Ni(0) in Ni(CO)<sub>4</sub> has a filled d shell in the VBT description. Square-planar [Ni(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2-</sup> also has all its d electrons paired.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which orbitals form the lower-energy set in an octahedral field?
solution: B - dxy, dxz and dyz The dxy, dxz and dyz orbitals lie between the ligand axes, so repulsion is smaller. These three form lower-energy t2g.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: How many unpaired electrons does an octahedral low-spin d<sup>5</sup> ion have?
solution: A - 1 With a large splitting, five electrons pair in t2g before occupying the higher set. The t2g<sup>5</sup> configuration leaves one unpaired electron.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: For octahedral d<sup>4</sup>, what is the high-spin configuration?
solution: D - t2g<sup>3</sup> e_g<sup>1</sup> In high-spin d<sup>4</sup>, the first three electrons occupy separate t2g orbitals. The fourth enters the higher set rather than pairing, giving t2g<sup>3</sup> eg<sup>1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which ligand generally causes the greatest octahedral splitting among the choices?
solution: D - CN<sup>-</sup> CN<sup>-</sup> is a strong-field ligand in the spectrochemical series and produces the greatest splitting among the given choices.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why is [Sc(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3+</sup> typically colourless in water?
options: Sc<sup>3+</sup> has five unpaired d electrons.
Its octahedral geometry prevents all absorption at every wavelength.
Sc<sup>3+</sup> has no d electrons for a d–d transition.
Water is a negatively charged ligand.
solution: C - Sc<sup>3+</sup> has no d electrons for a d–d transition. Sc<sup>3+</sup> is d<sup>0</sup>. Without a d electron available to be excited between split d levels, the aqua ion has no d–d colour.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which change generally increases splitting in an octahedral Co(III) complex?
options: Decrease the formal metal charge while keeping all else the same.
Replace fluoride by cyanide at fixed oxidation state.
solution: C - Replace fluoride by cyanide at fixed oxidation state. CN<sup>-</sup> lies higher than F<sup>-</sup> in the spectrochemical series. At the same Co(III) oxidation state it generally raises Δo.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In a metal carbonyl, which orbital of CO receives metal electron density during π back-bonding?
solution: D - An empty π* orbital Electron density flows from a filled metal d orbital into an empty CO π* orbital. Occupying π* can weaken the internal C–O bond.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which phenomenon typically increases stability when a multidentate ligand replaces comparable monodentate ligands?
solution: A - Chelate effect A multidentate ligand forms more than one bond to the same centre and closes chelate rings. Such binding generally increases stability compared with analogous monodentate ligands.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the central metal in chlorophyll?
solution: A - Mg Chlorophyll has Mg<sup>2+</sup> coordinated in a nitrogen-containing macrocyclic ring.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which ligand is commonly used in complexometric determination of water hardness?
solution: B - EDTA EDTA forms stable complexes with Ca<sup>2+</sup> and Mg<sup>2+</sup>. In a hardness titration its 1:1 binding measures their combined amount.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each ligand with its typical denticity or binding description.
Column I
Column II
P. H2O
1. Often up to six donor atoms
Q. Ethane-1,2-diamine
2. One donor atom through O
R. Oxalato
3. Two donor atoms through N
S. EDTA4-
4. Two donor atoms through O
solution: D - P–2, Q–3, R–4, S–1 Water binds once through O, en twice through N, oxalato twice through O, and EDTA can bind through six atoms.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each formula with the metal oxidation state.
Column I
Column II
P. [Co(NH3)5Cl]2+
1. 0
Q. [Ni(CO)4]
2. +2
R. [Fe(CN)6]4-
3. +3
S. [PtCl6]2-
4. +4
solution: B - P–3, Q–1, R–2, S–4 With NH<sub>3</sub> and CO neutral, Cl<sup>-</sup> or CN<sup>-</sup> each −1, balance the complex charges to get Co +3, Ni 0, Fe +2 and Pt +4.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each formula with the coordination number of the metal.
Column I
Column II
P. [Ag(NH3)2]+
1. 4
Q. [PtCl4]2-
2. 8
R. [Fe(CN)6]3-
3. 6
S. [ZrF8]4-
4. 2
solution: C - P–4, Q–1, R–3, S–2 All the stated ligands are monodentate. Counting them gives 2 for Ag, 4 for Pt, 6 for Fe and 8 for Zr.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each arrangement change with the corresponding isomerism.
Column I
Column II
P. Different donor atom of the same ligand
1. Linkage
Q. Exchange between coordination sphere and
counter-ion
2. Ionisation
R. Different relative positions of ligands
3. Optical
S. Non-superimposable mirror images
4. Geometrical
solution: D - P–1, Q–2, R–4, S–3 The four changes affect donor atom, inner versus outer ion, spatial position and mirror-image handedness. They give linkage, ionisation, geometrical and optical isomerism.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match the hybridisation with its usual VBT description.
Column I
Column II
P. sp
1. Tending to linear
Q. sp3
2. Tetrahedral
R. dsp2
3. Square planar
S. d2sp3
4. Inner-orbital octahedral
solution: C - P–1, Q–2, R–3, S–4 The VBT assignments are sp for linear, sp<sup>3</sup> for tetrahedral, dsp<sup>2</sup> for square planar, and d<sup>2</sup>sp<sup>3</sup> for inner-orbital octahedral geometry.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each example with number of unpaired metal d electrons in the stated geometry
and field.
Column I
Column II
P. [Ni(CN)4]2-, square planar
1. 2
Q. [Ti(H2O)6]3+, d1
2. 5
R. [NiCl4]2-, tetrahedral
3. 1
S. [FeF6]3-, high-spin d5
4. 0
solution: C - P–4, Q–3, R–1, S–2 Square-planar Ni(II) cyanide has 0 unpaired, Ti(III) d<sup>1</sup> has 1, tetrahedral Ni(II) d<sup>8</sup> has 2, and high-spin Fe(III) d<sup>5</sup> has 5.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each description with the relevant arrangement.
Column I
Column II
P. Two identical ligands adjacent in a square plane
1. cis
Q. Two identical ligands opposite in a square plane
2. mer
R. Three identical ligands on one octahedral face
3. trans
S. Three identical ligands in a meridian with an
opposite pair
4. fac
solution: B - P–1, Q–3, R–4, S–2 Adjacent identical ligands are cis and opposite ones trans. A facial trio is mutually cis. A meridional trio includes a trans pair.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each Werner complex with moles of immediately precipitable AgCl from one mole
of complex.
Column I
Column II
P. [Co(NH3)6]Cl3
1. 3
Q. [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2
2. 0
R. [Co(NH3)4Cl2]Cl
3. 1
S. [Co(NH3)3Cl3]
4. 2
solution: A - P–1, Q–4, R–3, S–2 Only chloride outside the square brackets precipitates immediately. Counting those ions in order gives 3, 2, 1 and 0 AgCl per formula unit.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each application or molecule with a characteristic complex.
Column I
Column II
P. Cancer chemotherapy
1. Cisplatin
Q. Photosynthesis pigment
2. Chlorophyll
R. Oxygen transport in blood
3. Haemoglobin
S. Water-hardness titration
4. Metal–EDTA complex
solution: A - P–1, Q–2, R–3, S–4 Cisplatin is a chemotherapy compound, chlorophyll absorbs light, haemoglobin binds oxygen, and EDTA complexes the hardness ions.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each bonding term with its description.
Column I
Column II
P. CO → metal σ donation
1. Electron pair donated by CO
Q. Metal → CO π back-donation
2. Ring formation by multiple attachments of one
ligand
R. Octahedral crystal-field splitting
3. Metal d electrons donated into CO π*
S. Chelation
4. Separation into lower t2g and higher eg sets
solution: B - P–1, Q–3, R–4, S–2 CO donates a lone pair to the metal, and metal d orbitals donate back to CO π*. The octahedral field splits d levels. Chelation closes a ring around the metal.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) In octahedral complexes, the eg set lies below the t2g set. Reason (R) Orbitals directed along the axes experience stronger repulsion from ligands on the axes.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. The eg orbitals point along the axes and experience greater repulsion, placing them above t2g.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Metal-to-CO back-bonding can weaken the internal C–O bond. Reason (R) It introduces electron density into an antibonding orbital of CO.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Filling CO antibonding π* reduces the C–O bond order, which explains the weakening.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A chelate can be more stable than a corresponding complex with monodentate ligands. Reason (R) The spectrochemical series ranks ligands by their crystal-field splitting effects.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. The chelate effect concerns multidentate binding and complex stability. The spectrochemical series concerns splitting and does not explain that effect.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) [Pt(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>] is tetrahedral in the standard cisplatin structure. Reason (R) Pt(II) in cisplatin has a square-planar environment.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Cisplatin has square-planar Pt(II), with the two chlorido ligands adjacent.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) [Co(en)<sub>3</sub>]<sup>3+</sup> has coordination number six. Reason (R) Each of its three en ligands provides two donor atoms.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Three bidentate en ligands supply 3 × 2 = 6 donor atoms.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) [Ni(CO)<sub>4</sub>] is tetrahedral. Reason (R) CO is electrically neutral.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. The absence of charge on CO fixes the oxidation-state calculation. Tetrahedral geometry follows from four-coordinate Ni(0) bonding, not merely the ligand’s charge.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) [Fe(CN)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>4-</sup> is low-spin and diamagnetic. Reason (R) Its six d electrons pair in the lower t2g orbitals in the strong ligand field.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Fe(II) is d<sup>6</sup> and CN<sup>-</sup> produces a large splitting. All six electrons pair in t2g, giving diamagnetism.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) The cis and trans forms of [Pt(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>] are geometrical isomers. Reason (R) These forms differ by the donor atom through which NH<sub>3</sub> binds.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Both ammine ligands bind through N in either isomer. Only the positions of the ligands change.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) SCN<sup>-</sup> can show linkage isomerism. Reason (R) It always attaches to a single metal through both N and S at the same time.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. SCN<sup>-</sup> can bind through either S or N in linkage isomers. Simultaneous attachment through both is not required.

heading: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 5 Coordination Compounds Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>6</sub>]Cl<sub>3</sub> contains three counter-ions per complex cation. Reason (R) The coordination number of cobalt is six.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. Three Cl<sup>-</sup> balance the +3 cation. Six ammine donors determine the coordination number independently.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which is a vinylic halide?
solution: D - CH<sub>2</sub>=CHCl The chlorine in CH<sub>2</sub>=CHCl is attached directly to one of the double-bond carbons, which makes it a vinylic halide.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In which compound is Cl bonded to an allylic carbon?
solution: B - CH<sub>2</sub>=CHCH<sub>2</sub>Cl In CH<sub>2</sub>=CH–CH<sub>2</sub>Cl the Cl-bearing sp<sup>3</sup> carbon is next to the double bond. That position is allylic.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound is a geminal dihalide?
solution: A - CH<sub>3</sub>CHCl<sub>2</sub> In CH<sub>3</sub>CHCl<sub>2</sub> both Cl atoms are bonded to the same carbon, the defining feature of a geminal dihalide.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)CH<sub>2</sub>Br?
solution: A - 1-Bromo-2-methylpropane The longest chain has three carbons. Number from the Br end to place bromo at C-1 and methyl at C-2.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound contains an aryl carbon–halogen bond?
solution: C - p-Bromotoluene In p-bromotoluene, Br is bonded directly to an aromatic ring carbon. That is an aryl C–Br bond.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which reagent gives chloroethane from ethanol and gaseous SO<sub>2</sub> and HCl as by-products?
solution: B - SOCl<sub>2</sub> Thionyl chloride converts ethanol to chloroethane: CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH + SOCl<sub>2</sub> → CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>Cl + SO<sub>2</sub> + HCl.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which alkyl halide is the final product of the Finkelstein reaction using 1-chloropropane?
solution: C - 1-Iodopropane In dry acetone, iodide displaces chloride at the primary carbon of 1-chloropropane. The product is CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>I.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What drives the Finkelstein reaction of a primary alkyl bromide with NaI in dry acetone?
options: NaI is precipitated as the main product.
Acetone is oxidised to an acid.
solution: A - NaBr precipitates. NaBr is poorly soluble in dry acetone and precipitates. Its removal favours formation of the alkyl iodide.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which reagent can be used in the Swarts reaction to prepare an alkyl fluoride?
solution: B - AgF Silver fluoride is a Swarts fluorinating reagent. It replaces the original halogen, forming an alkyl fluoride.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product is favoured when propene reacts with HBr in the presence of peroxides?
solution: D - 1-Bromopropane Peroxide starts radical addition. Br adds to the end of propene to generate the more stable secondary carbon radical, leading to terminal bromination.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which propyl halide has the weakest C–X bond?
solution: B - 1-Iodopropane Iodine is the largest halogen of the usual comparison. The longer C–I bond is weaker than the corresponding C–Cl or C–Br bonds.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound usually has the highest boiling point?
solution: D - Iodomethane Iodomethane has the most polarisable electron cloud among methyl halides. Stronger London dispersion forces give it the highest boiling point in the group.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why does p-dichlorobenzene have an unusually high melting point among its positional isomers?
options: Its symmetry allows efficient crystal packing.
It has the largest molecular mass.
It has a different molecular formula.
solution: A - Its symmetry allows efficient crystal packing. The para isomer is more symmetrical and packs efficiently in a crystal, so more energy is needed to disrupt its solid lattice.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product forms predominantly when 1-bromopropane is heated with aqueous KOH?
solution: D - Propan-1-ol Aqueous OH<sup>-</sup> acts as a nucleophile and replaces Br at the primary carbon, yielding CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which major alkene forms from 2-bromobutane with hot alcoholic KOH?
solution: B - But-2-ene Hot alcoholic KOH favours β-elimination. Removing HBr preferentially makes the more substituted alkene, but-2-ene, by Zaitsev orientation.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which is the major organic product when chloroethane reacts with alcoholic KCN?
solution: C - Propanenitrile KCN supplies CN<sup>-</sup> that attacks mainly through carbon. Replacement of Cl adds a carbon to the chain and forms CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CN.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which is the major organic product when chloroethane reacts with AgCN?
solution: C - Ethyl isocyanide With largely covalent AgCN, the N end is the effective nucleophilic site in the textbook treatment. The product is CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>NC.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What does 1-bromopropane form with Mg in dry ether?
solution: B - Propylmagnesium bromide Mg inserts into the C–Br bond under anhydrous ether conditions to form CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>MgBr.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which undergoes SN2 fastest with the same nucleophile and solvent?
solution: C - Bromomethane A methyl carbon offers the least steric hindrance for backside attack. That makes bromomethane the best SN2 substrate here.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which alkyl halide is best suited to SN1 solvolysis in a suitable polar protic solvent?
solution: B - 2-Chloro-2-methylpropane The tertiary substrate can ionise to a relatively stable tert-butyl carbocation. The polar protic solvent stabilises the ions formed.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the stereochemical result of a clean SN2 at an optically active carbon when configuration is compared by geometry?
options: No change because attack is frontside
Racemisation caused by a free carbocation
solution: C - Inversion at the reacting carbon The nucleophile attacks from the side opposite the departing group. The geometry at the centre inverts, whether or not the R/S label changes.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which species is typically involved in the slow ionisation step of SN1?
options: Formation of a carbon radical pair through homolysis
Formation of a carbocation and a leaving-group ion
solution: C - Formation of a carbocation and a leaving-group ion In the slow SN1 step, the C–leaving-group bond ionises. This gives a carbocation and a leaving-group ion before nucleophilic capture.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why is chlorobenzene’s C–Cl bond shorter than the bond in a comparable chloroalkane?
options: Resonance gives partial double-bond character, and the bonded carbon is sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised.
The chloride group is ionised in the ground state.
There is no electronic interaction between Cl and the aromatic ring.
Chlorobenzene contains an sp<sup>3</sup> carbon bonded to Cl.
solution: A - Resonance gives partial double-bond character, and the bonded carbon is sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised. Chlorine lone-pair donation gives the aryl bond partial double-bond character. The sp<sup>2</sup> carbon also forms a shorter bond than a comparable sp<sup>3</sup> carbon.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which substituent at the para position most strongly facilitates the usual nucleophilic aromatic substitution of chlorobenzene?
solution: A - NO<sub>2</sub> A para NO<sub>2</sub> group withdraws electron density and delocalises the negative charge of the addition intermediate, favouring nucleophilic aromatic substitution.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which products dominate when chlorobenzene is nitrated?
solution: D - o- and p-Nitrochlorobenzene Chlorine withdraws inductively and deactivates the ring, but lone-pair resonance stabilises the ortho and para substitution intermediates.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product is associated with coupling bromobenzene and methyl bromide with sodium in dry ether?
solution: B - Toluene Wurtz–Fittig coupling joins the phenyl group of bromobenzene to the methyl group of methyl bromide, giving toluene.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which reaction of bromoethane with sodium in dry ether gives butane?
solution: B - Wurtz reaction Two ethyl groups couple with sodium in dry ether to give CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>. This alkyl–alkyl coupling is the Wurtz reaction.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product can result when two molecules of chlorobenzene couple with sodium in dry ether?
solution: C - Biphenyl Coupling two aryl units is a Fittig reaction. Two phenyl groups join to give C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>–C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound is dichloromethane?
solution: D - CH<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub> Dichloromethane has two chlorines and two hydrogens attached to one carbon, CH<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which polyhalogen compound is commonly called iodoform?
solution: D - CHI<sub>3</sub> Iodoform is triiodomethane, CHI<sub>3</sub>. It is the yellow precipitate in the iodoform test.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each compound with its halide class.
Column I
Column II
P. CH2=CHCl
1. Benzylic
Q. CH2=CHCH2Cl
2. Vinylic
R. C6H5CH2Cl
3. Aryl
S. C6H5Cl
4. Allylic
solution: A - P–2, Q–4, R–1, S–3 Cl is attached directly to a double-bond carbon, next to a double bond, next to an aromatic ring, or directly to an aromatic ring, respectively.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each formula with its name.
Column I
Column II
P. CH3CH2Br
1. 2-Bromopropane
Q. CH3CHBrCH3
2. Bromoethane
R. CH3CH2CH2Br
3. 1-Bromopropane
S. CH2Br2
4. Dibromomethane
solution: D - P–2, Q–1, R–3, S–4 The formulas have two carbons, Br at C-2 of propane, Br at C-1 of propane, and two Br atoms on methane, in that order.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each reagent or condition with the usual outcome.
Column I
Column II
P. NaI in dry acetone with R–Br
1. Alkyl fluoride
Q. AgF with R–Cl
2. Grignard reagent
R. Mg and dry ether with R–Br
3. Alkyl chloride plus SO2 and HCl
S. SOCl2 with a primary alcohol
4. Alkyl iodide
solution: C - P–4, Q–1, R–2, S–3 NaI effects iodide exchange, AgF gives fluoride exchange, Mg inserts into R–Br, and SOCl<sub>2</sub> gives R–Cl with SO<sub>2</sub> and HCl.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each reaction name with a representative reactant combination.
Column I
Column II
P. Wurtz
1. An aryl and an alkyl halide with Na
Q. Fittig
2. Diazonium salt with a suitable Cu(I) halide
R. Wurtz–Fittig
3. Two aryl halide units with Na
S. Sandmeyer
4. Two alkyl halide units with Na
solution: A - P–4, Q–3, R–1, S–2 Wurtz couples alkyl–alkyl, Fittig aryl–aryl, Wurtz–Fittig aryl–alkyl, and Sandmeyer uses a diazonium salt with a suitable Cu(I) reagent.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each treatment of bromoethane with its principal organic product.
Column I
Column II
P. Aqueous KOH
1. Ethanol
Q. Hot alcoholic KOH
2. Ethyl isocyanide
R. Alcoholic KCN
3. Ethene
S. AgCN
4. Propanenitrile
solution: A - P–1, Q–3, R–4, S–2 Aqueous OH<sup>-</sup> gives ethanol, hot alcoholic KOH gives ethene, KCN bonds through C to give propanenitrile, and AgCN gives ethyl isocyanide.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each mechanistic feature with its usual description.
Column I
Column II
P. Backside attack
1. Carbocation formation in SN1
Q. Slow ionisation
2. Inversion in SN2
R. Concerted displacement
3. Attack from either face is possible
S. A planar cation at a stereogenic centre
4. Single step in SN2
solution: D - P–2, Q–1, R–4, S–3 Backside attack gives inversion. Slow ionisation produces the SN1 carbocation. SN2 is concerted, whereas a planar carbocation admits attack from either face.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each structure with its classification.
Column I
Column II
P. CH3CH2CH2Br

Q. CH3CHBrCH3
2. Tertiary alkyl halide
R. (CH3)3CBr
3. Secondary alkyl halide
S. CH3Br
4. Primary alkyl halide
solution: A - P–4, Q–3, R–2, S–1 Count carbon neighbours of the Br-bearing carbon. There are 1, 2, 3 and 0, giving primary, secondary, tertiary and methyl, respectively.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each familiar name with its formula.
Column I
Column II
P. Methylene chloride
1. CHI3
Q. Chloroform
2. CHCl3
R. Carbon tetrachloride
3. CCl4
S. Iodoform
4. CH2Cl2
solution: C - P–4, Q–2, R–3, S–1 Methylene chloride is CH<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>, chloroform CHCl<sub>3</sub>, carbon tetrachloride CCl<sub>4</sub> and iodoform CHI<sub>3</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each observation with its interpretation.
Column I
Column II
P. Higher melting point of p-dichlorobenzene
1. More efficient crystal packing
Q. Slow substitution at an unactivated aryl chloride
2. Zaitsev orientation
R. Faster SN2 for a methyl halide
3. Low steric hindrance
S. More substituted alkene usually favoured
4. Strong C(sp2)–Cl bond with resonance contribution
solution: D - P–1, Q–4, R–3, S–2 Efficient packing raises the para isomer’s melting point. A strengthened aryl bond resists ordinary substitution, minimal crowding favours methyl SN2, and Zaitsev orientation favours substitution on the double bond.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each conversion with a suitable reagent or condition.
Column I
Column II
P. Chlorobenzene to phenol
1. HBr with peroxide
Q. Benzene to chlorobenzene
2. Cl2 with anhydrous FeCl3
R. Propene to 2-bromopropane
3. HBr without peroxide
S. Propene to 1-bromopropane
4. Hot pressurised aqueous NaOH then acidification
solution: B - P–4, Q–2, R–3, S–1 Hot pressurised NaOH gives phenoxide, then acid gives phenol. Cl<sub>2</sub>/FeCl<sub>3</sub> chlorinates benzene, and HBr orientation changes from Markovnikov to anti-Markovnikov with peroxide.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) p-Dichlorobenzene has a higher melting point than its ortho isomer. Reason (R) Its more symmetrical structure packs efficiently in the solid.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. The more symmetrical para isomer packs efficiently, thereby raising the crystal melting point.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) An optically active reacting centre can undergo inversion in an SN2 displacement. Reason (R) The nucleophile attacks from the side opposite the leaving group.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Backside approach opposite the departing group inverts the arrangement around the reacting carbon.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A para nitro group facilitates nucleophilic substitution of chlorobenzene. Reason (R) It can stabilise the anionic intermediate by electron withdrawal and resonance.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Negative charge in the addition intermediate can delocalise into the para nitro group, which facilitates substitution.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Alcoholic KOH often favours elimination of an alkyl halide on heating. Reason (R) The usual alkene-forming pathway is nucleophilic addition to an aromatic ring.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. A base removes a β-hydrogen while the leaving group is lost, generating an alkene.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) The Finkelstein reaction can use NaI in dry acetone. Reason (R) Its driving force is precipitation of NaI, the reagent used.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. It is the product salt NaBr or NaCl that precipitates, helping drive the exchange.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) 1-Bromobutane usually undergoes SN1 faster than tert-butyl bromide in the same medium. Reason (R) A tertiary carbocation is more stable than a simple primary carbocation.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. tert-Butyl bromide ionises more readily because the tertiary carbocation is more stable.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Chlorobenzene has no resonance contribution involving the C–Cl bond. Reason (R) One lone pair on chlorine can conjugate with the aromatic π system.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
