solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Conjugation of a chlorine lone pair gives a resonance contribution with extra C–Cl bond order.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Bromoethane can give propanenitrile with KCN. Reason (R) Bromoethane can also undergo elimination with hot alcoholic KOH.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. KCN allows carbon-end nucleophilic substitution. Hot alcoholic KOH promotes a separate elimination pathway.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Chlorobenzene gives mainly ortho and para products on nitration. Reason (R) Its C–Cl bond is shorter than an alkyl C–Cl bond.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. Lone-pair resonance stabilises the ortho and para nitration intermediates. Bond length does not explain the orientation.

heading: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Dry ether is used for the formation of a Grignard reagent. Reason (R) Water stabilises Grignard reagents against decomposition.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Water protonates and destroys RMgX, producing RH. The ether medium must be dry.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which is a benzylic alcohol?
solution: D - C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH The OH-bearing carbon in C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH lies next to an aromatic ring. That makes it benzylic.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which name corresponds to (CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>CHCH<sub>2</sub>OH?
solution: B - 2-Methylpropan-1-ol The longest chain containing the OH-bearing carbon has three carbons. Numbering from OH gives propan-1-ol with a methyl substituent at C-2.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the IUPAC name of C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OCH<sub>3</sub>?
solution: D - Methoxyethane For CH<sub>3</sub>OCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub> the longer ethyl group supplies the ethane parent. The shorter CH<sub>3</sub>O– group is named methoxy.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which alcohol contains two hydroxy groups?
solution: B - Ethane-1,2-diol The suffix diol means two hydroxy groups. Ethane-1,2-diol has one on each carbon, HOCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound is a tertiary alcohol?
solution: B - 2-Methylbutan-2-ol In 2-methylbutan-2-ol the OH-bearing carbon is bonded to two methyl groups and one ethyl group, making it tertiary.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which alcohol forms by hydroboration–oxidation of but-1-ene?
solution: A - Butan-1-ol Hydroboration places boron on the less substituted terminal carbon. Oxidation replaces B with OH at that carbon, producing butan-1-ol.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which alcohol forms predominantly by acid-catalysed hydration of but-1-ene?
solution: A - Butan-2-ol In acid hydration the favoured intermediate is the secondary carbocation at C-2. Water adds there to give the Markovnikov product.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which carbonyl compound gives a primary alcohol on reaction with a Grignard reagent and subsequent hydrolysis?
solution: D - Methanal Methanal has two H atoms on the carbonyl carbon. Adding one R group and protonating the alkoxide gives RCH<sub>2</sub>OH, a primary alcohol.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which reagents give butan-2-ol by Grignard addition followed by hydrolysis?
solution: A - Ethanal and C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>MgBr The ethanal carbonyl carbon already bears CH<sub>3</sub> and H. Adding C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub> from the Grignard reagent and hydrolysing gives CH<sub>3</sub>CH(OH)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which order of boiling points is expected for these substances?
solution: A - Propane < methoxyethane < propan-1-ol Propane relies on dispersion forces. Methoxyethane also has dipole interactions. Propan-1-ol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds and boils highest.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why does water solubility generally fall from ethanol to hexan-1-ol?
options: The number of hydroxy groups increases.
The nonpolar alkyl portion becomes larger.
solution: C - The nonpolar alkyl portion becomes larger. Both alcohols have only one OH group, but the longer hydrocarbon chain in hexan-1-ol is less compatible with water, lowering solubility.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which is the most acidic among the following?
solution: C - p-Nitrophenol The para nitro group withdraws electron density by induction and resonance, stabilising the phenoxide conjugate base and increasing acidity.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound gives sodium phenoxide on treatment with aqueous NaOH?
solution: A - Phenol Phenol can transfer its proton to aqueous OH<sup>-</sup>. The resonance-stabilised anion remains as sodium phenoxide.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What gas evolves when ethanol is treated with metallic sodium?
solution: B - H<sub>2</sub> Sodium replaces the hydroxyl hydrogen. The products are sodium ethoxide and hydrogen: 2C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH + 2Na → 2C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>ONa + H<sub>2</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which ester forms from ethanol and propanoic acid in acid-catalysed esterification?
solution: D - Ethyl propanoate Propanoic acid supplies the propanoate portion and ethanol supplies the ethyl group. Acid-catalysed condensation removes water.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product forms predominantly when ethanol is heated at about 413 K with concentrated H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>?
solution: C - Ethoxyethane At around 413 K the textbook conditions favour intermolecular dehydration of two ethanol molecules, yielding C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OC<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What does protonation achieve in acid-catalysed dehydration of an alcohol?
options: Converts OH into a hydride ion.
Makes the substrate a stronger base.
Turns OH into a better leaving group as water.
Adds oxygen permanently to the carbon chain.
solution: C - Turns OH into a better leaving group as water. Protonation converts the OH group into an attached OH<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup> group. It can then depart as neutral water, a better leaving group.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which starting alcohol gives an aldehyde on controlled dehydrogenation over Cu at 573 K?
solution: D - Butan-1-ol A primary alcohol loses H from the O–H bond and the carbon carrying OH. Butan-1-ol therefore gives butanal.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which organic product forms from propan-2-ol vapour over hot Cu at 573 K?
solution: D - Propanone Heating a secondary alcohol over Cu removes H<sub>2</sub>. Dehydrogenation of CH<sub>3</sub>CH(OH)CH<sub>3</sub> forms CH<sub>3</sub>COCH<sub>3</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which alcohol gives immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent at room temperature?
solution: B - 2-Methylpropan-2-ol The tertiary alcohol forms its tert-butyl chloride rapidly in Lucas reagent. The insoluble chloride produces immediate turbidity.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product precipitates when phenol reacts with bromine water?
solution: D - 2,4,6-Tribromophenol The OH group strongly activates the ring. Bromination in water occurs at both ortho positions and at para, producing a white precipitate.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which products dominate when phenol is nitrated with dilute HNO<sub>3</sub>?
solution: A - 2-Nitrophenol and 4-nitrophenol Dilute nitric acid gives principally the ortho and para mononitration products because OH donates electron density into the ring by resonance.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product is obtained by heating phenol with zinc dust?
solution: A - Benzene Zinc dust removes oxygen from phenol on heating, yielding benzene and ZnO.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which functional group is introduced during the Reimer–Tiemann reaction of phenol?
solution: B - A formyl group Reimer–Tiemann formylation installs –CHO, mainly ortho to OH. After workup the principal product is salicylaldehyde.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which organic salt is carboxylated in Kolbe’s reaction before acidification to salicylic acid?
solution: A - Sodium phenoxide Sodium phenoxide reacts with CO<sub>2</sub> under pressure to give mainly sodium salicylate. Acidification converts it into salicylic acid.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which laboratory combination is better suited to the Williamson preparation of methyl tert-butyl ether?
solution: C - Sodium tert-butoxide and methyl iodide tert-Butoxide attacks methyl iodide by SN2. A tertiary alkyl halide as electrophile would instead be prone to elimination.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which bond is cleaved preferentially in anisole on heating with HI?
options: One carbon–carbon bond of the ring
solution: A - The methyl–oxygen bond I<sup>-</sup> attacks the methyl group of protonated anisole by SN2. Cleavage of the methyl–oxygen bond gives CH<sub>3</sub>I and phenol.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the principal aromatic product of anisole bromination in ethanoic acid?
solution: D - p-Bromoanisole The methoxy group directs bromination ortho and para. The less crowded para product is the principal one.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which alcohol is called wood spirit?
solution: C - Methanol Methanol is conventionally called wood spirit because it was historically obtained by destructive distillation of wood.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: How many moles of ethyl iodide can one mole of ethoxyethane form with excess hot HI?
solution: B - 2 The first equivalent of HI gives ethyl iodide and ethanol. Excess hot HI converts that ethanol to a second equivalent of ethyl iodide.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each structure with its IUPAC name.
Column I
Column II
P. CH3CH2OH
1. Propan-2-ol
Q. (CH3)2CHOH
2. Ethanol
R. (CH3)3COH
3. Methoxyethane
S. CH3OCH2CH3
4. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol
solution: A - P–2, Q–1, R–4, S–3 The structures contain an OH on ethane, OH at C-2 of propane, OH and methyl at C-2 of propane, and methoxy on ethane, respectively.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each process with its principal product.
Column I
Column II
P. Propene plus water under acid catalysis
1. Propan-1-ol
Q. Propene by hydroboration then oxidation
2. Propan-2-ol
R. Propanone plus CH3MgBr then hydrolysis
3. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol
S. Ethanal plus C2H5MgBr then hydrolysis
4. Butan-2-ol
solution: C - P–2, Q–1, R–3, S–4 Acid hydration marks the more substituted carbon. Hydroboration–oxidation marks the less substituted one. Methyl addition to propanone and ethyl addition to ethanal give the two stated alcohols.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each treatment with its characteristic outcome.
Column I
Column II
P. Phenol with neutral FeCl3
1. White precipitate
Q. Tertiary alcohol with Lucas reagent
2. Immediate turbidity at room temperature
R. Phenol with bromine water
3. Hydrogen evolution
S. Ethanol with Na
4. Violet colour
solution: B - P–4, Q–2, R–1, S–3 FeCl<sub>3</sub> gives a violet phenol complex, Lucas reagent gives rapid turbidity with a tertiary alcohol, bromine water gives a white precipitate, and sodium liberates H<sub>2</sub> from ethanol.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each conversion of phenol with a suitable reagent or condition.
Column I
Column II
P. Phenol to salicylaldehyde
1. Strong nitrating conditions
Q. Phenol to salicylic acid
2. CO2 under pressure with sodium phenoxide then
acidification
R. Phenol to benzene
3. Heat with zinc dust
S. Phenol to picric acid
4. CHCl3 and aqueous NaOH then acidification
solution: D - P–4, Q–2, R–3, S–1 CHCl<sub>3</sub>/base formylates phenol. CO<sub>2</sub> fixes onto sodium phenoxide, zinc removes oxygen, and strong nitration yields the trinitro compound picric acid.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each alcohol with the expected class of product on passing its vapour over Cu at
573 K, or with its separate stated transformation.
Column I
Column II
P. Propan-1-ol over Cu
1. Alkene
Q. Propan-2-ol over Cu
2. Ketone
R. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol over Cu
3. Aldehyde
S. Ethanol with propanoic acid and H+
4. Ester
solution: D - P–3, Q–2, R–1, S–4 Primary and secondary alcohols dehydrogenate to aldehydes and ketones. The tertiary alcohol dehydrates to an alkene. Ethanol and propanoic acid give an ester.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match the ether reaction with its product or observation.
Column I
Column II
P. Anisole with hot HI
1. Phenol and CH3I
Q. Ethoxyethane with excess hot HI
2. Two ethyl iodide molecules per ether
R. Anisole with Br2 in ethanoic acid
3. Anisole
S. Sodium phenoxide plus CH3I
4. Mainly para bromo product
solution: C - P–1, Q–2, R–4, S–3 Hot HI gives phenol and CH<sub>3</sub>I from anisole, and two ethyl iodides from diethyl ether with excess acid. Bromination favours para. Phenoxide methylation yields anisole.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each pair of reagents with the expected ether.
Column I
Column II
P. CH3ONa and CH3I
1. 2-Methoxy-2-methylpropane
Q. C2H5ONa and CH3I
2. Ethoxyethane
R. C2H5ONa and C2H5Br
3. Methoxyethane
S. (CH3)3CONa and CH3I
4. Methoxymethane
solution: B - P–4, Q–3, R–2, S–1 In each case the alkoxide O bonds to the alkyl group from the halide. The four products are dimethyl, methyl ethyl, diethyl and methyl tert-butyl ether.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match the molecular feature with its consequence.
Column I
Column II
P. Intermolecular hydrogen bonding in alcohols
1. Greater acidity than cyclohexanol
Q. Intramolecular hydrogen bonding in o-nitrophenol
2. Higher boiling point than comparable ethers
R. Resonance delocalisation in phenoxide
3. Lower solubility in water
S. Larger nonpolar alkyl group
4. Greater steam volatility than the para isomer
solution: C - P–2, Q–4, R–1, S–3 Alcohol intermolecular hydrogen bonds raise boiling point. Internal bonding aids steam volatility of o-nitrophenol, resonance stabilises phenoxide, and a longer alkyl group reduces aqueous solubility.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match the material or term with its description.
Column I
Column II
P. Wood spirit
1. Methoxybenzene
Q. Denatured spirit
2. Methanol
R. Glycerol
3. Propane-1,2,3-triol
S. Anisole
4. Ethanol made unfit for drinking by additives
solution: C - P–2, Q–4, R–3, S–1 Wood spirit is methanol, denatured spirit is ethanol made unfit for drinking, glycerol is a three-OH propane, and anisole is methoxybenzene.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each process with its name.
Column I
Column II
P. Sodium alkoxide plus primary alkyl halide to ether
1. Fischer esterification
Q. Carboxylation of sodium phenoxide
2. Williamson synthesis
R. Formylation of phenol with CHCl3 and base
3. Kolbe reaction
S. Alcohol plus carboxylic acid under acid catalysis
4. Reimer–Tiemann reaction
solution: B - P–2, Q–3, R–4, S–1 Alkoxide alkylation is Williamson, CO<sub>2</sub> fixation on phenoxide is Kolbe, phenol formylation is Reimer–Tiemann and acid-catalysed alcohol–acid condensation is Fischer esterification.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Propan-1-ol boils at a higher temperature than methoxyethane. Reason (R) Propan-1-ol molecules can form intermolecular O–H hydrogen bonds with one another.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. The O–H groups of propan-1-ol form intermolecular hydrogen bonds, increasing the energy needed for vaporisation.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Anisole gives mainly ortho and para products on electrophilic substitution. Reason (R) It can be prepared from sodium phenoxide and methyl iodide.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. Resonance donation of a methoxy oxygen lone pair explains orientation. A route used to synthesise anisole does not explain the orientation.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Acid-catalysed dehydration starts with protonation of the alcohol oxygen. Reason (R) This step makes the leaving group hydroxide rather than water.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Protonation makes the departing group water. An unprotonated OH group would be a poor leaving group.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Hot HI cleaves anisole to phenol and methyl iodide. Reason (R) The aromatic sp<sup>2</sup> carbon undergoes facile backside substitution by I<sup>-</sup>.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. I<sup>-</sup> attacks the methyl carbon. Ordinary SN2 backside substitution does not occur at the aryl sp<sup>2</sup> carbon.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Propan-2-ol can be oxidised to propanone. Reason (R) Propan-2-ol lacks a hydrogen on the carbon carrying OH.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. The middle carbon bears a hydrogen. Oxidation removes that H and the hydroxyl H to form the ketone.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Phenol is more acidic than cyclohexanol. Reason (R) Phenoxide is stabilised by resonance, unlike cyclohexoxide.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Phenoxide delocalises its negative charge by resonance, stabilising the conjugate base relative to cyclohexoxide.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) p-Nitrophenol is generally more steam-volatile than o-nitrophenol. Reason (R) o-Nitrophenol can form an intramolecular hydrogen bond.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Intramolecular bonding reduces intermolecular association in o-nitrophenol, making it more steam-volatile than the para isomer.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Phenol yields a white precipitate with bromine water. Reason (R) Phenol forms a coloured complex with neutral ferric chloride.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. The precipitate is 2,4,6-tribromophenol. The FeCl<sub>3</sub> colour comes from a separate complexation reaction.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) An alkoxide and a tertiary alkyl bromide are generally preferred for a clean Williamson synthesis. Reason (R) Strong alkoxide base can favour elimination with tertiary alkyl halides.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. A tertiary halide is hindered for SN2 and often eliminates with strong alkoxide. A methyl or suitable primary electrophile is preferred.

heading: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Hydroboration–oxidation of but-1-ene gives butan-1-ol. Reason (R) The overall transformation places OH at the less substituted carbon of the original double bond.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. The overall regiochemistry places OH at the terminal, less substituted carbon, giving butan-1-ol.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound is named 3-methylbutanal?
solution: A - CH<sub>3</sub>CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)CH<sub>2</sub>CHO The aldehyde carbon is C-1. A four-carbon parent with a methyl substituent at C-3 gives CH<sub>3</sub>CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)CH<sub>2</sub>CHO.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound is pentan-3-one?
solution: D - CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>COCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub> Pentan-3-one is a five-carbon ketone with the carbonyl at C-3. Both sides of the carbonyl are ethyl groups.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which feature attracts a nucleophile to the carbonyl group?
options: Partial negative charge on carbonyl carbon
An unpaired electron on oxygen in the ground state
Partial positive charge on carbonyl carbon
solution: D - Partial positive charge on carbonyl carbon Oxygen draws density from the C=O bond, making oxygen partially negative and the carbonyl carbon partially positive. The nucleophile attacks that carbon.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which carbonyl compound usually reacts most readily in nucleophilic addition?
solution: A - Methanal Methanal has the least crowded carbonyl and no alkyl groups donating electron density. It is generally the most reactive for nucleophilic addition among these choices.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product is obtained from ethanal and hydroxylamine?
solution: A - Ethanal oxime Hydroxylamine adds and the intermediate loses water, replacing C=O by C=NOH. The product is CH<sub>3</sub>CH=NOH.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the product type when propanone reacts with HCN?
solution: D - Cyanohydrin CN<sup>-</sup> adds at the carbonyl carbon. Protonation yields (CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>C(OH)CN, a cyanohydrin.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Ethanal reacts with two equivalents of ethanol in dry HCl. What is the organic product under acetal-forming conditions?
solution: C - 1,1-Diethoxyethane Under dry acid, the aldehyde first forms a hemiacetal, then substitutes its OH with another ethoxy group. The acetal is CH<sub>3</sub>CH(OC<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>)<sub>2</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which pair can both give an orange or yellow precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent?
solution: B - Propanal and butan-2-one Both aldehydes and ketones react with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine, giving the corresponding coloured hydrazone precipitates.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is deposited in a positive Tollens’ test?
solution: D - Metallic silver The aldehyde reduces the diamminesilver(I) ion to elemental Ag, which deposits as a silver mirror.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound usually gives a positive Fehling’s test?
solution: A - Butanal Butanal is an aliphatic aldehyde. It reduces the blue Cu(II) complex to brick-red Cu<sub>2</sub>O in the standard Fehling’s test.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound gives a positive iodoform test?
solution: D - Butan-2-one Butan-2-one contains the CH<sub>3</sub>CO– group required for a methyl ketone to yield yellow CHI<sub>3</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which substrate does not undergo ordinary self-aldol condensation?
solution: C - Benzaldehyde Benzaldehyde has no hydrogen on a carbon adjacent to C=O that can form the requisite enolate. It therefore cannot undergo ordinary self-aldol addition.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which is the initial aldol addition product of ethanal?
solution: A - 3-Hydroxybutanal An ethanal enolate attacks a second ethanal molecule. Protonation gives CH<sub>3</sub>CH(OH)CH<sub>2</sub>CHO, with the new OH on C-3.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which organic products form when benzaldehyde undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction in concentrated NaOH?
solution: B - Benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate Two benzaldehyde molecules disproportionate. One is reduced to benzyl alcohol and the other is oxidised to benzoate, present as its sodium salt in NaOH.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which reagent reduces propanone to propan-2-ol?
solution: C - NaBH<sub>4</sub> NaBH<sub>4</sub> delivers hydride to the ketone carbonyl. The resulting alkoxide is protonated to give propan-2-ol.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which set of reagents corresponds to Clemmensen reduction?
solution: A - Zn(Hg) and concentrated HCl Amalgamated zinc and concentrated HCl reduce the carbonyl group to CH<sub>2</sub> under acidic Clemmensen conditions.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product forms when acetophenone undergoes Wolff–Kishner reduction?
solution: D - Ethylbenzene Hydrazone formation followed by base and heat replaces the carbonyl by CH<sub>2</sub>. C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>COCH<sub>3</sub> thus becomes C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which catalyst is used to reduce an acid chloride to an aldehyde by Rosenmund reduction?
solution: A - Pd supported on BaSO<sub>4</sub> Rosenmund hydrogenation uses Pd on BaSO<sub>4</sub>, typically moderated to limit further reduction of the resulting aldehyde.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which reagent in Stephen reduction converts a nitrile to an intermediate that gives an aldehyde on hydrolysis?
solution: C - SnCl<sub>2</sub>/HCl SnCl<sub>2</sub>/HCl partially reduces the nitrile to an imine salt. Hydrolysis of that intermediate gives the aldehyde.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which reagent is characteristic of the Etard oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde followed by hydrolysis?
solution: B - Chromyl chloride Chromyl chloride, CrO<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>, reacts with the benzylic methyl group. Hydrolysis of the Etard intermediate yields benzaldehyde.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound is obtained after oxidation of ethylbenzene with hot alkaline KMnO<sub>4</sub> and then acidification?
solution: A - Benzoic acid Ethylbenzene has benzylic hydrogen. Hot permanganate oxidises the side chain to benzoate, which gives benzoic acid on acidification.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which gas is observed when ethanoic acid reacts with NaHCO<sub>3</sub>?
solution: A - CO<sub>2</sub> Acid protonates bicarbonate to give carbonic acid, which decomposes into H<sub>2</sub>O and CO<sub>2</sub>. The CO<sub>2</sub> causes the effervescence.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which is most acidic in water?
solution: C - Trichloroacetic acid Three chlorine atoms strongly withdraw electron density by induction, stabilising trichloroacetate and increasing acidity.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What stabilises a carboxylate ion relative to the alkoxide ion of a comparable alcohol?
options: Formation of a permanent positive charge on oxygen
Complete localisation of the charge on carbon
Absence of lone pairs on oxygen
Delocalisation of negative charge over two oxygen atoms
solution: D - Delocalisation of negative charge over two oxygen atoms The two resonance contributors of a carboxylate distribute negative charge between both oxygen atoms. In the comparable alkoxide, the charge is localised on one O.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound forms on reaction of propanoic acid with SOCl<sub>2</sub>?
solution: B - Propanoyl chloride SOCl<sub>2</sub> replaces the acid OH with Cl, forming CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>COCl along with SO<sub>2</sub> and HCl.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which ester forms from methanol and ethanoic acid on acid-catalysed esterification?
solution: B - Methyl ethanoate Methanol gives the methyl group attached to O and ethanoic acid gives the ethanoate portion. The product is CH<sub>3</sub>COOCH<sub>3</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product forms during soda-lime decarboxylation of sodium butanoate?
solution: C - Propane Soda lime removes the carboxyl carbon from the salt. The remaining three-carbon chain becomes CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which organic product forms when propanoic acid undergoes the Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction with Br<sub>2</sub> and red P?
solution: B - 2-Bromopropanoic acid The Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction replaces an α-hydrogen by Br. Propanoic acid gives CH<sub>3</sub>CHBrCOOH.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the product of acidic hydrolysis of propanenitrile?
solution: C - Propanoic acid Acidic hydrolysis converts –CN through an amide to –COOH. Including the nitrile carbon, the chain remains three carbons long.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why do many carboxylic acids boil higher than aldehydes of similar molar mass?
options: Aldehydes always ionise fully in the pure liquid.
Aldehydes make stronger O–H hydrogen bonds with each other.
Carboxylic acids associate through intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
Carboxylic acids are normally monatomic gases.
solution: C - Carboxylic acids associate through intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Two carboxylic acid molecules can form a cyclic dimer with two intermolecular hydrogen bonds. Strong association raises the boiling point.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each formula with its name.
Column I
Column II
P. CH3CHO
1. Ethanal
Q. CH3COCH3
2. Propanone
R. C6H5CHO
3. Benzaldehyde
S. CH3CH2COOH
4. Propanoic acid
solution: B - P–1, Q–2, R–3, S–4 CH<sub>3</sub>CHO is ethanal, CH<sub>3</sub>COCH<sub>3</sub> is propanone, C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>CHO is benzaldehyde and CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>COOH is propanoic acid.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each addition reagent with product type.
Column I
Column II
P. HCN
1. Hydrazone
Q. NH2OH
2. Oxime
R. NH2NH2
3. Semicarbazone
S. Semicarbazide
4. Cyanohydrin
solution: D - P–4, Q–2, R–1, S–3 HCN adds CN and OH across the carbonyl. The three nitrogen reagents replace the carbonyl O by C=N–OH, C=N–NH<sub>2</sub> or the semicarbazone group, respectively.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each observation with its test.
Column I
Column II
P. Silver mirror
1. 2,4-DNP
Q. Brick-red Cu2O
2. Tollens’
R. Pale-yellow CHI3
3. Fehling’s
S. Orange or yellow hydrazone precipitate
4. Iodoform
solution: B - P–2, Q–3, R–4, S–1 Tollens’ gives elemental silver, Fehling’s gives Cu<sub>2</sub>O, iodoform gives CHI<sub>3</sub>, and 2,4-DNP gives the coloured hydrazone.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each name reaction with its characteristic change.
Column I
Column II
P. Rosenmund
1. Nitrile to aldehyde
Q. Etard
2. Toluene to benzaldehyde
R. Stephen
3. Aldehyde disproportionation
S. Cannizzaro
4. Acid chloride to aldehyde
solution: D - P–4, Q–2, R–1, S–3 Rosenmund reduces an acid chloride, Etard oxidises a benzylic methyl group, Stephen partially reduces a nitrile, and Cannizzaro disproportionates a suitable aldehyde.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each reduction reagent with its use.
Column I
Column II
P. NaBH4
1. Clemmensen reduction
Q. Zn(Hg) and HCl
2. Controlled reduction of a nitrile to aldehyde
R. Hydrazine and base
3. Carbonyl to alcohol
S. DIBAL-H followed by hydrolysis
4. Wolff–Kishner reduction
solution: C - P–3, Q–1, R–4, S–2 NaBH<sub>4</sub> gives alcohols; Zn(Hg)/HCl is Clemmensen. Hydrazine/base is Wolff–Kishner. And controlled DIBAL-H reduction, then hydrolysis, can give an aldehyde from a nitrile.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each compound with its diagnostic behaviour under usual school tests.
Column I
Column II
P. Ethanoic acid
1. Iodoform positive with no 2,4-DNP precipitate
Q. Propanone
2. Fehling’s positive and iodoform negative
R. Propanal
3. CO2 with NaHCO3
S. Ethanol
4. Iodoform positive and Tollens’ negative
solution: A - P–3, Q–4, R–2, S–1 The acid releases CO<sub>2</sub>, propanone gives iodoform and is Tollens’ negative, propanal reacts with Fehling’s but lacks a methyl carbonyl group, and ethanol gives iodoform after oxidation but is initially 2,4-DNP negative.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match the carboxylic acid conversion with a suitable condition.
Column I
Column II
P. Benzoic acid to benzoyl chloride
1. SOCl2
Q. Propanoic acid to 2-bromopropanoic acid
2. Heat with soda lime
R. Ethanoic acid to ethyl ethanoate
3. Ethanol and catalytic H2SO4
S. Sodium propanoate to ethane
4. Br2 and red phosphorus, then hydrolysis
solution: B - P–1, Q–4, R–3, S–2 SOCl<sub>2</sub> gives the acid chloride, Br<sub>2</sub>/red P gives α-bromination, ethanol/acid forms the ester, and soda lime removes a carboxyl carbon from the salt.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each transformation of ethanal with its product.
Column I
Column II
P. Dilute base at low temperature
1. 3-Hydroxybutanal
Q. Aldol condensation followed by dehydration
2. But-2-enal
R. Oxidation with suitable oxidant
3. Ethanol
S. Reduction with NaBH4
4. Ethanoic acid
solution: C - P–1, Q–2, R–4, S–3 Cold dilute base gives the β-hydroxy aldehyde. Dehydration gives but-2-enal, oxidation gives ethanoic acid, and hydride reduction gives ethanol.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match the substituent with its role in the comparison indicated.
Column I
Column II
P. Cl in chloroacetic acid compared with acetic acid
1. Usually lowers electrophilicity and adds steric
hindrance
Q. Extra alkyl group on a ketone relative to an
aldehyde
2. Permits enolate formation
R. OH on a carboxyl group
3. Enables intermolecular H bonding
S. Alpha hydrogen in ethanal
4. Raises acidity by induction
solution: D - P–4, Q–1, R–3, S–2 Chlorine raises acidity by induction. An extra ketone alkyl group lowers electrophilicity and increases steric hindrance. COOH can hydrogen-bond, and the α-H enables enolate formation.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each substance with a widely used application or form.
Column I
Column II
P. Formaldehyde in water
1. Vinegar
Q. Acetone
2. Food preservative
R. Ethanoic acid in dilute water
3. Formalin
S. Sodium benzoate
4. Common organic solvent
solution: B - P–3, Q–4, R–1, S–2 Formalin is aqueous formaldehyde, acetone is a common solvent, dilute aqueous acetic acid is vinegar, and sodium benzoate is used as a preservative.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Propanone gives a positive iodoform test. Reason (R) Propanone can also be reduced to propan-2-ol.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. Iodoform formation depends on the CH<sub>3</sub>CO– group. The separate reduction of propanone to propan-2-ol does not explain it.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Benzaldehyde can undergo the Cannizzaro reaction. Reason (R) It lacks an alpha hydrogen for normal self-aldol addition.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. With no α-H, benzaldehyde cannot participate in normal self-aldol addition and fits the class of aldehydes that disproportionate in concentrated base.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Acid chlorides can be converted to aldehydes by Rosenmund reduction. Reason (R) The usual product is obtained by vigorous oxidation with KMnO<sub>4</sub>.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Rosenmund is catalytic hydrogenation, using H<sub>2</sub> and a moderated Pd/BaSO<sub>4</sub> catalyst.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Ethanal gives an aldol product in dilute NaOH. Reason (R) Ethanal also forms an oxime with hydroxylamine.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. The α-H permits enolate formation and aldol addition. Oxime formation with hydroxylamine is a separate reaction.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Ethanoic acid produces effervescence with NaHCO<sub>3</sub>. Reason (R) O<sub>2</sub> is the gas responsible for the effervescence.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. The gas is CO<sub>2</sub>, released after bicarbonate is protonated.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Controlled reduction of a nitrile can provide an aldehyde. Reason (R) Carboxylic acids can also be prepared by hydrolysis of nitriles.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. Controlled reduction can stop at an aldehyde after hydrolysis of its intermediate. Direct hydrolysis of a nitrile is a distinct route to a carboxylic acid.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Trichloroacetic acid is stronger than acetic acid. Reason (R) Chlorine atoms stabilise the conjugate base by their electron-withdrawing inductive effect.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. The chlorines pull electron density inductively, stabilising trichloroacetate and increasing acidity.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Propanone usually gives a silver mirror with Tollens’ reagent. Reason (R) Typical aldehydes are readily oxidised by Tollens’ reagent.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Propanone is an ordinary ketone and does not give the Tollens’ mirror. Typical aldehydes reduce silver(I) while being oxidised.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Pentan-3-one gives a positive standard iodoform test. Reason (R) A ketone needs a methyl group directly attached to the carbonyl carbon for this test.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. In pentan-3-one both groups on C=O are ethyl, so it lacks the directly attached methyl required for a ketone to give the test.

heading: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Carboxylic acids often have higher boiling points than comparable aldehydes. Reason (R) Carboxylic acids can form intermolecular hydrogen-bonded dimers.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Hydrogen-bonded dimers increase intermolecular association, raising the temperature needed to vaporise the acid.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which formula represents a tertiary amine?
solution: D - N(CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>3</sub> A tertiary amine has three carbon groups directly bonded to N and no N–H bond. Trimethylamine has three methyl groups.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which name represents CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>NHCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
solution: A - N-Ethylethanamine Choose ethanamine as the parent and name the ethyl group attached to N as an N-ethyl substituent.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound is a primary aromatic amine?
solution: B - C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>NH<sub>2</sub> In aniline the N is bonded directly to a phenyl ring and bears two hydrogens. This makes it a primary aromatic amine.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product forms on complete reduction of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CN with LiAlH<sub>4</sub> and then hydrolysis?
solution: A - Propan-1-amine LiAlH<sub>4</sub> reduces the nitrile group to –CH<sub>2</sub>NH<sub>2</sub> after work-up. The nitrile carbon remains in the chain, giving three carbons in total.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which combination can convert nitrobenzene to aniline after work-up?
solution: B - Sn/HCl followed by basification Tin and hydrochloric acid reduce –NO<sub>2</sub> to the protonated amine. Adding base on work-up releases free aniline.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What product forms in Hoffmann bromamide degradation of benzamide?
solution: C - Aniline In the Hoffmann reaction the phenyl group migrates to N via an isocyanate. Hydrolysis and loss of the original carbonyl carbon give C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>NH<sub>2</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Compared with the amide, how many carbons are in the amine produced by the Hoffmann bromamide reaction?
solution: A - One fewer The amide carbonyl carbon is lost during conversion of RCONH<sub>2</sub> to RNH<sub>2</sub>. The final amine therefore contains one fewer carbon.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which organic reagent is used in Gabriel synthesis to form a salt that undergoes alkylation?
solution: A - Phthalimide Phthalimide loses its acidic N–H proton to form a nucleophilic salt. Its anion alkylates a suitable haloalkane, and subsequent cleavage releases the primary amine.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why is an excess of NH<sub>3</sub> used when making an amine by ammonolysis of a haloalkane?
options: It favours exclusive formation of a quaternary salt.
It blocks nucleophilic substitution at carbon.
It favours formation of primary amine over further alkylation.
solution: D - It favours formation of primary amine over further alkylation. Excess ammonia competes with the amine product for reaction with the haloalkane, favouring first alkylation and limiting formation of more highly alkylated amines.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which normally has the lowest boiling point among these C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>9</sub>N isomers?
solution: D - Trimethylamine Trimethylamine lacks N–H bonds and cannot donate hydrogen bonds to its own molecules. The other comparable amine isomers can associate through N–H hydrogen bonding.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What accounts for solubility of lower amines in water?
options: Formation of metallic bonds with water
An inability to accept hydrogen bonds
solution: C - Hydrogen bonding with water The N lone pair can accept a hydrogen bond from water. Primary and secondary amines can also donate through their N–H bonds.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which is the weakest base among the choices in aqueous solution?
solution: B - p-Nitroaniline The para nitro group withdraws electron density by induction and resonance. It makes aniline’s N lone pair even less available for accepting a proton.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why is the lone pair on aniline less available for protonation than that on cyclohexylamine?
options: Aniline has no lone pair on nitrogen.
Its nitrogen has a permanent positive charge.
The C–N bond in aniline is purely ionic.
It is delocalised into the benzene ring.
solution: D - It is delocalised into the benzene ring. Aniline’s N lone pair overlaps with the aromatic π system. In cyclohexylamine the lone pair is localised and more readily accepts H<sup>+</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which has the higher basic strength in aqueous solution among ethylamine and diethylamine under comparable conditions?
options: Both have exactly the same basic strength
solution: B - Diethylamine Aqueous basic strength depends on inductive donation and solvation of the conjugate acid. For these two ethylamines the net result favours diethylamine.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which amine gives a positive carbylamine test?
solution: D - Propan-1-amine The carbylamine test requires a primary amine with an –NH<sub>2</sub> group. Propan-1-amine is the primary amine listed.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which compound is the major product when aniline reacts with CHCl<sub>3</sub> and alcoholic KOH in the carbylamine test?
solution: D - Phenyl isocyanide Aniline, a primary aromatic amine, reacts with chloroform and alcoholic KOH to give C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>NC, phenyl isocyanide.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product in the Hinsberg test dissolves in alkali because it retains an acidic N–H?
options: Sulfonamide derived from a secondary amine
Sulfonamide derived from a primary amine
A tertiary amine sulfonamide with one N–H bond
A tertiary amine sulfonamide with two N–H bonds
solution: B - Sulfonamide derived from a primary amine A primary amine forms RNH–SO<sub>2</sub>C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub> and retains an N–H proton. Alkali removes it to make an ionic, soluble sulfonamide salt.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the initial outcome for triethylamine with Hinsberg reagent and aqueous alkali under the usual test conditions?
options: It does not form a sulfonamide.
It gives a sulfonamide with one acidic N–H.
It gives a sulfonamide that cannot dissolve in dilute acid.
solution: B - It does not form a sulfonamide. Triethylamine has no N–H bond and does not form a sulfonamide under the standard Hinsberg test conditions.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the usual first organic product from methanamine and nitrous acid in water?
solution: A - Methanol The unstable methyldiazonium intermediate loses N<sub>2</sub>. Reaction in water gives CH<sub>3</sub>OH.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What explains keeping diazotisation of aniline near 273–278 K?
options: Sodium nitrite cannot dissolve above 278 K.
Ice converts the diazonium ion directly to phenol.
Aniline is a solid at every higher temperature.
Aromatic diazonium salts are more stable at low temperature.
solution: D - Aromatic diazonium salts are more stable at low temperature. Cooling to about 273–278 K slows decomposition of the aryl diazonium salt. It can then be used for substitution or coupling.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product forms when benzenediazonium chloride reacts with aqueous KI?
solution: C - Iodobenzene Iodide replaces the diazonium group, releasing N<sub>2</sub> and producing C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>I. Copper is unnecessary in this usual iodide substitution.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which reagent replaces the diazonium group with CN in the Sandmeyer reaction?
solution: C - CuCN CuCN supplies the cyano group in Sandmeyer substitution, converting the aryl diazonium group to –CN with loss of N<sub>2</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product forms on warming benzenediazonium chloride with water?
solution: B - Phenol Heating the diazonium salt with water replaces –N<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup> by –OH. Phenol forms and N<sub>2</sub> escapes.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product forms by treating benzenediazonium chloride with H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>2</sub>?
solution: B - Benzene Hypophosphorous acid reduces the diazonium group to hydrogen. C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>N<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup> is therefore converted into benzene.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which transformation commonly uses benzenediazonium tetrafluoroborate as intermediate?
solution: A - Aniline to fluorobenzene In the Balz–Schiemann reaction the aryl diazonium tetrafluoroborate is heated. It decomposes to fluorobenzene with loss of N<sub>2</sub> and BF<sub>3</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which product precipitates when aniline is treated with bromine water?
solution: D - 2,4,6-Tribromoaniline The amino group strongly activates ortho and para positions. Bromine water replaces three ring hydrogens to give a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why is the amino group acetylated before monobromination in a route to p-bromoaniline?
options: It removes nitrogen from the molecule.
It makes the ring exclusively meta-directing.
It makes bromine water a reducing agent.
It moderates activation and limits polysubstitution.
solution: D - It moderates activation and limits polysubstitution. Acetylation makes acetanilide, whose nitrogen lone pair is also shared with the carbonyl. This reduces activation and favours mainly para monobromination.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the principal product type of benzenediazonium chloride and phenol under suitable coupling conditions?
solution: B - An azo compound The diazonium ion couples with activated phenol to give an aromatic –N=N– linkage. In mildly alkaline medium, the main product is para-coupled.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why can direct nitration of aniline yield appreciable meta substitution?
options: Some aniline is protonated in the strongly acidic medium.
The unprotonated NH<sub>2</sub> group is strongly meta-directing.
The diazonium ion is always formed first.
NO<sub>2</sub> always substitutes meta in benzene derivatives.
solution: A - Some aniline is protonated in the strongly acidic medium. Strong acid protonates some aniline to the anilinium ion, C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>NH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>. This deactivating substituent directs electrophilic substitution meta.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why does aniline generally fail to undergo ordinary Friedel–Crafts alkylation with AlCl<sub>3</sub>?
options: It cannot form any complex with AlCl<sub>3</sub>.
The amino group binds AlCl<sub>3</sub> and deactivates the aromatic ring.
The amino group is replaced directly by aluminium.
solution: C - The amino group binds AlCl<sub>3</sub> and deactivates the aromatic ring. Aniline coordinates through its N lone pair to the Lewis-acid catalyst AlCl<sub>3</sub>. Complex formation strongly deactivates the ring toward ordinary Friedel–Crafts reaction.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each amine with its classification.
Column I
Column II
P. CH3NH2
1. Primary aromatic
Q. C2H5NHCH3
2. Tertiary aliphatic
R. N(CH3)3
3. Primary aliphatic
S. C6H5NH2
4. Secondary aliphatic
solution: C - P–3, Q–4, R–2, S–1 Count carbon groups bonded to N: 1, 2, 3 and 1. The one-group phenyl example is aromatic, and the other three are aliphatic.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each formula with its IUPAC name.
Column I
Column II
P. CH3NH2
1. N-Methylethanamine
Q. CH3CH2NH2
2. Ethanamine
R. CH3CH(NH2)CH3
3. Propan-2-amine
S. CH3CH2NHCH3
4. Methanamine
solution: D - P–4, Q–2, R–3, S–1 The structures contain methyl, ethyl, propan-2-yl, and ethyl plus N-methyl groups, giving the four corresponding amine names.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each preparation with its representative product.
Column I
Column II
P. CH3CN reduction
1. Ethylamine
Q. Nitrobenzene reduction
2. Butan-1-amine
R. Butanamide with Br2/NaOH
3. Aniline
S. Gabriel synthesis using 1-bromobutane
4. Propan-1-amine
solution: C - P–1, Q–3, R–4, S–2 Nitrile reduction retains C to give ethylamine, nitro reduction gives aniline, Hoffmann degradation loses C to give propan-1-amine, and Gabriel synthesis preserves the butyl chain.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each reagent with its role.
Column I
Column II
P. CHCl3 and alcoholic KOH
1. Diazotisation of aniline
Q. Benzenesulfonyl chloride
2. White precipitate formation
R. NaNO2 and HCl, cold
3. Hinsberg test
S. Bromine water with aniline
4. Carbylamine test
solution: A - P–4, Q–3, R–1, S–2 Chloroform and alcoholic base are used in carbylamine. Benzenesulfonyl chloride is the Hinsberg reagent, cold nitrite/acid diazotises, and bromine water gives tribromoaniline precipitate.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each diazonium substitution with a suitable reagent.
Column I
Column II
P. Diazonium group to Cl
1. CuCl/HCl
Q. Diazonium group to Br
2. KI
R. Diazonium group to I
3. CuBr/HBr
S. Diazonium group to F
4. HBF4 followed by heating
solution: C - P–1, Q–3, R–2, S–4 CuCl/HCl gives chlorobenzene, CuBr/HBr gives bromobenzene, KI supplies iodide, and heating the tetrafluoroborate formed using HBF<sub>4</sub> gives fluorobenzene.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each diazonium reaction with its product.
Column I
Column II
P. With CuCN
1. Mainly p-hydroxyazobenzene
Q. Warm water
2. Benzonitrile
R. With H3PO2
3. Benzene
S. With phenol in mildly alkaline medium
4. Phenol
solution: C - P–2, Q–4, R–3, S–1 The substitutions with CuCN and warm water give benzonitrile and phenol. H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>2</sub> gives benzene and phenol under coupling conditions gives mainly p-hydroxyazobenzene.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each amine with its expected Hinsberg behaviour.
Column I
Column II
P. Ethylamine
1. The free amine dissolves as an ammonium salt
Q. Diethylamine
2. Sulfonamide soluble in alkali
R. Triethylamine
3. No sulfonamide under test conditions
S. Triethylamine remaining after the test, then dilute
HCl
4. Sulfonamide insoluble in alkali
solution: A - P–2, Q–4, R–3, S–1 The primary sulfonamide has an acidic N–H and dissolves in alkali. The secondary sulfonamide has no N–H and stays insoluble. Triethylamine forms no sulfonamide but dissolves on acidification as a salt.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each situation with the relevant explanation.
Column I
Column II
P. Aniline weaker base than methylamine
1. Resonance delocalisation of N lone pair
Q. Primary amine often higher boiling than tertiary
isomer
2. Intermolecular N–H hydrogen bonding
R. Lower amines dissolve in water
3. Solute–water hydrogen bonding
S. Aliphatic diazonium ions are short-lived in water
4. Rapid loss of N2
solution: A - P–1, Q–2, R–3, S–4 Aniline loses lone-pair availability by resonance. Primary amines self-associate via N–H hydrogen bonds, lower amines hydrogen-bond to water, and aliphatic diazonium ions lose N<sub>2</sub> quickly.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each step with its purpose or outcome.
Column I
Column II
P. Acetylation of aniline
1. Protect the amino group and temper ring
activation
Q. Bromination of acetanilide
2. Regenerate free amino group
R. Hydrolysis of p-bromoacetanilide
3. Introduce the diazonium group
S. Diazotisation of aniline
4. Predominantly para substitution
