solution: C - P–1, Q–4, R–2, S–3 Acetylation protects and reduces activation, bromination chiefly substitutes para, hydrolysis restores NH<sub>2</sub>, and diazotisation installs –N<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each transformation with its name.
Column I
Column II
P. Benzamide to aniline with Br2/base
1. Sandmeyer reaction
Q. Alkyl halide to primary amine via phthalimide
2. Azo coupling
R. Diazonium chloride to chlorobenzene with CuCl
3. Hoffmann bromamide degradation
S. Diazonium salt plus phenol to coloured organic
product
4. Gabriel synthesis
solution: B - P–3, Q–4, R–1, S–2 Br<sub>2</sub>/base degrades benzamide by Hoffmann, phthalimide alkylation gives Gabriel, CuCl substitution is Sandmeyer, and reaction with phenol forms an azo bond.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Ethylamine gives N<sub>2</sub> with nitrous acid. Reason (R) The primary aliphatic diazonium intermediate is stable at room temperature.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. The primary aliphatic diazonium intermediate is unstable and decomposes with evolution of N<sub>2</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Hoffmann bromamide degradation of propanamide gives ethylamine. Reason (R) The carbonyl carbon stays in the final amine as a methylene group.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Propanamide loses its carbonyl carbon and gives two-carbon ethylamine. The carbonyl carbon does not enter the amine.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) N-Methylaniline does not give the carbylamine test. Reason (R) The test is given only by tertiary amines.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. N-Methylaniline is secondary, whereas only primary amines give a positive carbylamine test.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Benzenediazonium chloride is prepared at low temperature. Reason (R) It can ultimately be converted to iodobenzene with KI.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. Cooling slows diazonium decomposition. Its subsequent conversion to iodobenzene is a distinct substitution and does not explain the preparation temperature.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Direct nitration of aniline in strongly acidic medium can give some meta product. Reason (R) Protonation converts NH<sub>2</sub> to NH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>, which directs substitution meta.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Protonation changes the ortho/para-directing –NH<sub>2</sub> group into meta-directing –NH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>, accounting for some meta product.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Gabriel synthesis readily prepares aniline from chlorobenzene under ordinary alkylation conditions. Reason (R) The reaction normally relies on nucleophilic substitution at an alkyl carbon.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Ordinary Gabriel alkylation requires displacement at an alkyl carbon. Chlorobenzene cannot undergo that standard SN2 step.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Gabriel synthesis generally gives a primary aliphatic amine. Reason (R) Aniline undergoes diazotisation with nitrous acid.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. Gabriel synthesis releases a primary aliphatic amine by cleavage of an N-alkylated imide. Aniline’s diazotisation is unrelated.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Triethylamine has an N–H bond and can donate a hydrogen bond. Reason (R) It has a lone pair on nitrogen and can accept a hydrogen bond.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Three ethyl groups occupy all N–H positions, but the amine retains a lone pair capable of accepting a hydrogen bond.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Acetylation helps control monobromination when making p-bromoaniline. Reason (R) The acylamino group activates the aromatic ring less strongly than the free amino group.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. The amide carbonyl shares the N lone pair, moderating ring activation and helping avoid multiple bromination.

heading: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 9 Amines Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Aniline is less basic in water than ethylamine. Reason (R) Aniline’s nitrogen lone pair is partly delocalised into the ring.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Resonance makes aniline’s lone pair less available for protonation than the localised lone pair of ethylamine in water.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which carbohydrate cannot be hydrolysed to a simpler carbohydrate?
solution: A - Ribose Ribose is a monosaccharide: it already consists of a single sugar unit and cannot be hydrolysed to a simpler carbohydrate.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which carbohydrate is an aldopentose?
solution: D - Ribose Ribose contains five carbons and has an aldehyde group in its open-chain form. These features make it an aldopentose.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which sugar is a ketohexose?
solution: D - Fructose Open-chain fructose contains six carbons and a ketone group, so it is a ketohexose.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What does formation of the pentaacetate of glucose indicate?
options: Five hydroxy groups are available for acetylation.
solution: B - Five hydroxy groups are available for acetylation. Acetylation converts each available OH into an acetate ester. A pentaacetate therefore demonstrates five acetylatable OH groups.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What does the formation of n-hexane on prolonged heating of glucose with HI support?
options: Two separate chains of three carbons
A straight chain of six carbon atoms
solution: C - A straight chain of six carbon atoms Conversion to n-hexane replaces oxygen-containing groups and preserves the carbon skeleton, supporting a continuous unbranched chain of six carbons.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which acid is formed when glucose is oxidised with bromine water under mild conditions?
solution: C - Gluconic acid Bromine water oxidises the open-chain aldehyde group at C-1 to a carboxylic acid without oxidising the terminal primary alcohol under these mild conditions.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: How do α-D-glucose and β-D-glucose differ in their cyclic forms?
options: Position of the terminal CH<sub>2</sub>OH group
solution: A - Configuration at C-1 Cyclisation creates an anomeric centre at the original carbonyl carbon, C-1. The α and β forms differ in the configuration of that centre.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which pair forms on hydrolysis of lactose?
solution: C - Glucose and galactose Hydrolysis of the β-(1→4) bond in lactose releases one galactose and one glucose molecule.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which sugar produces two D-glucose molecules on complete hydrolysis?
solution: D - Maltose Maltose consists of two glucose units joined through an α-(1→4) glycosidic linkage. Hydrolysis separates the two units.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why does sucrose fail to reduce Tollens’ reagent under the usual test conditions?
options: Both anomeric carbons are involved in its glycosidic linkage.
Only its glucose unit is joined through a non-anomeric carbon.
solution: A - Both anomeric carbons are involved in its glycosidic linkage. The linkage between glucose C-1 and fructose C-2 locks both anomeric centres. Sucrose lacks a free reducing end able to form an open-chain carbonyl under the test conditions.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which glycosidic linkage forms the main chain of amylose?
solution: C - α-(1→4) Amylose is largely unbranched and links α-glucose residues from the anomeric C-1 of one unit to C-4 of the next.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which linkage is present at branch points of amylopectin?
solution: C - α-(1→6) The primary chain is α-(1→4), but branching links an anomeric C-1 to C-6 of another glucose unit.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the main carbohydrate storage polymer in animals?
solution: A - Glycogen Glycogen is a highly branched glucose polymer stored especially in animal liver and muscle.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which polymer forms a major part of plant cell walls?
solution: B - Cellulose Cellulose, a linear β-(1→4) glucose polymer, forms strong fibres that provide plant cell walls with structural support.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which functional group makes up the peptide linkage?
solution: D - –CO–NH– The carboxyl group of one residue links to the amino group of the next with loss of water, forming an amide bond, –CO–NH–.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is the number of peptide bonds in an open-chain tetrapeptide?
solution: A - 3 An open chain of n amino acid residues has n − 1 peptide links. For four residues there are three links.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which structure is the zwitterion form of alanine?
solution: B - <sup>+</sup>H<sub>3</sub>N–CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)–COO<sup>-</sup> Internal proton transfer produces the ammonium group –NH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup> and a carboxylate –COO<sup>-</sup> on the same molecule, giving the zwitterion shown.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which amino acid is essential in the human diet?
solution: D - Valine Valine is essential because humans cannot synthesise enough of it and must obtain it from the diet.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What does a protein’s primary structure specify?
options: Regular folding such as a β-sheet
solution: D - Amino acid sequence The primary structure is the specific order of residues along the polypeptide backbone.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What is an α-helix an example of in proteins?
solution: B - Secondary structure An α-helix is a local regular conformation stabilised by hydrogen bonds between backbone groups. Such local folding is secondary structure.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What changes on denaturation under conditions that leave peptide bonds intact?
options: Chemical identity of all amino acids
solution: A - Native higher-order folding Denaturation disrupts interactions stabilising secondary, tertiary or quaternary structure. Where peptide bonds remain intact, the primary sequence is preserved.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What role do most enzymes play?
options: They are consumed stoichiometrically in the net reaction.
They increase the standard Gibbs energy change.
They increase the equilibrium constant at fixed temperature.
They lower kinetic barriers to particular reactions.
solution: D - They lower kinetic barriers to particular reactions. Enzymes are catalysts. They lower the activation barrier of particular reactions and speed the approach to equilibrium.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which vitamin is associated with night blindness when deficient?
solution: D - Vitamin A Vitamin A is needed to make retinal for the visual pigment used in dim-light vision. Deficiency can therefore cause night blindness.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which pair contains two fat-soluble vitamins?
solution: A - A and E Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. Both A and E belong to that group.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which deficiency condition is associated with vitamin B<sub>1</sub>?
solution: B - Beriberi Vitamin B<sub>1</sub> is thiamine. Its severe deficiency is associated with beriberi.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which one of the following is absent from a nucleoside but present in a nucleotide?
solution: D - A phosphate group A nucleoside contains a nitrogenous base and sugar. Adding a phosphate group gives a nucleotide.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which component is characteristic of RNA rather than DNA in the usual comparison?
solution: C - Ribose RNA uses ribose, with an OH at C-2′. DNA uses 2′-deoxyribose, which has H at that position.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: How many hydrogen bonds form in a standard G–C base pair in DNA?
solution: B - 3 The standard guanine–cytosine pair aligns three donor–acceptor combinations for hydrogen bonding.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which hormone generally raises the concentration of glucose in blood?
solution: C - Glucagon Glucagon promotes glucose release into the blood, for example by stimulating breakdown of liver glycogen.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Where do two complementary strands in the usual DNA double helix interact most directly?
options: Between bases via glycosidic bonds between strands
Between sugar residues via peptide bonds
Between phosphate groups via ester bonds between strands
Between paired nitrogenous bases via hydrogen bonds
solution: D - Between paired nitrogenous bases via hydrogen bonds The outward sugar–phosphate backbones belong to their separate strands. Hydrogen bonds between complementary bases pair the strands internally.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each sugar with its classification.
Column I
Column II
P. D-Glucose
1. Ketohexose
Q. D-Fructose
2. Aldohexose
R. D-Ribose
3. Aldopentose
S. Sucrose
4. Disaccharide
solution: A - P–2, Q–1, R–3, S–4 Glucose is a six-carbon aldose, fructose a six-carbon ketose, ribose a five-carbon aldose, and sucrose contains two linked monosaccharides.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each carbohydrate with its complete hydrolysis product or products.
Column I
Column II
P. Sucrose
1. Many glucose units per polymer chain
Q. Lactose
2. Glucose and fructose
R. Maltose
3. Glucose and galactose
S. Cellulose
4. Two glucose units per molecule
solution: A - P–2, Q–3, R–4, S–1 Hydrolysis yields glucose/fructose from sucrose, glucose/galactose from lactose, two glucoses from maltose, and many glucose units from cellulose.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each carbohydrate with its characteristic linkage or structure.
Column I
Column II
P. Amylose
1. Linear β-(1→4) glucose chain
Q. Amylopectin
2. Glycosidic bond involving both anomeric carbons
R. Cellulose
3. α-(1→4) chain with α-(1→6) branches
S. Sucrose
4. Mostly unbranched α-(1→4) glucose chain
solution: B - P–4, Q–3, R–1, S–2 Amylose is mainly unbranched α-(1→4). Amylopectin has α-(1→6) branches, cellulose is linear β-(1→4), and sucrose links both anomeric carbons.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each outcome with the structural inference about glucose it supports.
Column I
Column II
P. Reduction to n-hexane
1. An aldehyde can give a carboxylic acid
Q. Oxime formation
2. Unbranched six-carbon skeleton
R. Oxidation with bromine water
3. Five hydroxy groups can be acetylated
S. Pentaacetate formation
4. Presence of a carbonyl group in the open-chain
form
solution: C - P–2, Q–4, R–1, S–3 n-Hexane reveals the six-carbon chain, oxime shows a carbonyl, bromine water oxidises the aldehyde, and pentaacetate shows five acetylatable OH groups.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each protein structure level with its description.
Column I
Column II
P. Primary
1. Association of multiple polypeptide chains
Q. Secondary
2. Order of amino acid residues
R. Tertiary
3. Overall three-dimensional shape of one chain
S. Quaternary
4. Local regular folds such as helices
solution: B - P–2, Q–4, R–3, S–1 Primary is sequence, secondary is local regular folding, tertiary is the overall fold of one chain, and quaternary describes multiple associated chains.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each amino acid or protein term with its description.
Column I
Column II
P. Zwitterion
1. Disruption of native folding without ordinary
peptide hydrolysis
Q. Essential amino acid
2. –CO–NH– linkage
R. Peptide bond
3. Must be supplied adequately by the diet
S. Denaturation
4. A form that carries positive and negative groups
solution: B - P–4, Q–3, R–2, S–1 A zwitterion bears both charge types, an essential amino acid is diet-required, the peptide bond is an amide link, and denaturation disrupts native folding.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each vitamin with a well-known deficiency condition.
Column I
Column II
P. Vitamin A
1. Night blindness
Q. Vitamin B1
2. Beriberi
R. Vitamin C
3. Scurvy
S. Vitamin D
4. Rickets in children
solution: C - P–1, Q–2, R–3, S–4 Vitamin A deficiency impairs dim-light vision. B<sub>1</sub> deficiency can cause beriberi, C deficiency scurvy, and D deficiency rickets in children.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each biomolecule with its role or feature.
Column I
Column II
P. Keratin
1. Helps lower blood glucose
Q. Haemoglobin
2. Fibrous structural protein
R. Amylase
3. Catalyses starch hydrolysis
S. Insulin
4. Globular protein that transports oxygen
solution: A - P–2, Q–4, R–3, S–1 Keratin is a fibrous structural protein, haemoglobin is a globular oxygen carrier, amylase catalyses starch hydrolysis, and insulin helps lower glucose.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each nucleic acid term with its feature.
Column I
Column II
P. Nucleoside
1. Base plus pentose sugar
Q. Nucleotide
2. Two hydrogen bonds in DNA
R. A–T pairing
3. Three hydrogen bonds in DNA
S. G–C pairing
4. Nucleoside plus phosphate
solution: B - P–1, Q–4, R–2, S–3 Adding phosphate to a nucleoside yields a nucleotide. In standard DNA, A–T pairs form two hydrogen bonds and G–C pairs form three.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each biochemical conversion or observation with the relevant term.
Column I
Column II
P. Sucrose hydrolysis yielding a mixture with
opposite optical rotation
1. Denaturation
Q. Two cyclic glucose forms differing at C-1
2. Inversion
R. Heat-induced loss of native egg-white protein
structure
3. Substrate specificity
S. Enzyme binding the substrate at a particular site
4. Anomerism
solution: C - P–2, Q–4, R–1, S–3 Inversion refers to the change of optical rotation on sucrose hydrolysis. Glucose forms differing at C-1 are anomers. Heat denatures protein, and active-site recognition gives substrate specificity.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Glycogen stores glucose in animals. Reason (R) Cellulose is a structural carbohydrate in plants.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. Glycogen is an animal storage polymer with α linkages. Cellulose is a separate plant structural polymer and does not explain glycogen storage.

heading: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
tag: 12th Ch 10 Biomolecules Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Lactose hydrolysis gives glucose and fructose. Reason (R) Sucrose hydrolysis gives glucose and fructose.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Lactose yields glucose and galactose, whereas sucrose yields glucose and fructose.
